The Booming Supplement Industry in the Netherlands: A Comprehensive Look at Growth, Innovation, and Consumer Trends  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
15:41:10 UTC
00:41:10 KST

Introduction
The Netherlands has emerged as one of Europe's most dynamic markets for dietary supplements, experiencing remarkable growth that shows no signs of slowing. What was once a niche sector serving primarily athletes and bodybuilders has transformed into a mainstream industry catering to health-conscious consumers across all demographics. From Amsterdam to Rotterdam, Dutch consumers are increasingly turning to vitamins, minerals, probiotics, and specialised nutritional products to complement their diets and support overall wellbeing. This surge in popularity reflects broader societal shifts towards preventative healthcare, wellness optimisation, and a growing awareness of nutrition's crucial role in maintaining good health. As the supplement industry continues its upward trajectory in the Netherlands, understanding the factors driving this growth, the regulatory landscape, and future trends becomes essential for stakeholders and consumers alike.
The Current State of the Dutch Supplement Market
The supplement industry in the Netherlands has witnessed exponential growth over the past decade, with market valuations reaching impressive figures. Recent industry analyses estimate the Dutch supplement market to be worth hundreds of millions of euros annually, with consistent year-on-year growth rates often exceeding 5-7%. This expansion places the Netherlands amongst the leading European markets for nutritional supplements, despite its relatively modest population of approximately 17 million people.
The diversity of products available has expanded considerably, moving far beyond traditional multivitamins. Today's Dutch consumers can choose from an extensive range including omega-3 fatty acids, vitamin D supplements, probiotics, plant-based protein powders, collagen supplements, adaptogenic herbs, and increasingly sophisticated formulations targeting specific health concerns. Both physical retailers and online platforms stock thousands of products, catering to every conceivable nutritional need and preference.
The demographic consuming these products has also broadened significantly. Whilst athletes and fitness enthusiasts remain important customer segments, middle-aged professionals, elderly individuals seeking to maintain vitality, and even younger consumers interested in preventative health now constitute substantial portions of the market. This diversification has fuelled innovation and created opportunities for specialised product development.
Key Drivers Behind the Industry's Growth
Several interconnected factors have contributed to the supplement industry's remarkable expansion in the Netherlands. Perhaps most significantly, there has been a fundamental shift in how Dutch society views health and wellness. Rather than simply treating illness, many individuals now proactively invest in maintaining and optimising their health. This preventative approach aligns perfectly with supplement consumption, which promises to fill nutritional gaps and support various bodily functions.
The ageing population presents another crucial growth driver. As the Netherlands, like much of Europe, experiences demographic shifts towards an older population, demand for supplements addressing age-related concerns has surged. Products supporting joint health, cognitive function, cardiovascular wellness, and bone density have all seen increased sales as Baby Boomers seek to maintain quality of life in their later years.
Digital transformation has revolutionised how consumers discover, research, and purchase supplements. The proliferation of health and wellness influencers on social media platforms, combined with easy access to nutritional information online, has educated consumers and normalised supplement use. E-commerce platforms have made purchasing convenient, often offering broader selections and competitive pricing compared to traditional brick-and-mortar stores.
The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated many of these trends dramatically. Concerns about immune health prompted unprecedented interest in supplements containing vitamin C, vitamin D, zinc, and other immune-supporting nutrients. This surge in awareness appears to have created lasting behaviour changes, with many consumers continuing their supplement regimens long after the pandemic's acute phase.
Additionally, lifestyle factors particular to modern Dutch society have played a role. The Netherlands' northern latitude means limited sunlight exposure during winter months, creating widespread vitamin D deficiency and driving supplement demand. Busy lifestyles and changing dietary patterns, including the rise of plant-based eating, have also led consumers to seek nutritional insurance through supplementation.
Regulatory Framework and Quality Standards
The Netherlands operates within the European Union's regulatory framework for food supplements, which provides robust consumer protections whilst allowing market access for legitimate products. The Dutch Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit, or NVWA) oversees supplement regulation, ensuring products meet safety standards and labelling requirements.
Under EU law, supplements are classified as foods rather than medicines, meaning they cannot make disease prevention or treatment claims. Manufacturers must ensure products are safe, accurately labelled, and do not contain prohibited substances or excessive levels of nutrients. The NVWA conducts regular market surveillance, testing products and taking enforcement action against non-compliant operators.
This regulatory environment has generally served consumers well, maintaining high standards whilst allowing innovation. However, challenges persist. The growth of online sales, particularly from suppliers based outside the EU, has made regulatory oversight more complex. Counterfeit products and supplements containing undeclared ingredients occasionally reach Dutch consumers through these channels, highlighting the importance of purchasing from reputable sources.
Industry organisations such as NPN (Nederlandse Poedervoeders en Premixen) and various quality certification schemes help promote best practices and provide additional assurance to consumers. Many Dutch supplement companies such as MyCore Supplements NL voluntarily submit to third-party testing and certification programmes that verify product quality, purity, and label accuracy.
Innovation and Product Development Trends
The Dutch supplement industry has demonstrated remarkable innovation, developing sophisticated products that address specific consumer needs. Personalisation represents perhaps the most significant trend, with companies offering customised supplement regimens based on individual health assessments, genetic testing, or lifestyle questionnaires. This approach moves beyond one-size-fits-all multivitamins towards targeted nutritional support.
Plant-based and vegan supplements have experienced explosive growth, reflecting the Netherlands' position as a global leader in plant-based food adoption. Consumers increasingly demand supplements free from animal-derived ingredients, driving reformulation of traditional products and development of innovative alternatives to fish oil, collagen, and other historically animal-sourced supplements.
Delivery mechanisms have also evolved significantly. Beyond traditional tablets and capsules, Dutch consumers can now choose from gummies, effervescent tablets, powders, liquids, and even supplement-infused foods and beverages. These alternative formats appeal particularly to younger consumers and those who struggle with swallowing pills.
Sustainability has become a crucial consideration in product development. Environmentally conscious Dutch consumers favour supplements with eco-friendly packaging, sustainably sourced ingredients, and ethical production practices. Companies highlighting their environmental credentials and transparency throughout the supply chain often enjoy competitive advantages.
Distribution Channels and Market Access
The Dutch supplement market is characterised by diverse and evolving distribution channels. Traditional pharmacies and drugstores remain important retail outlets, with chains like Kruidvat and Etos dedicating substantial shelf space to supplements. These outlets benefit from consumer trust and the ability to provide face-to-face advice, though their product ranges may be more limited than specialised retailers.
Health food shops and specialised supplement stores offer extensive selections and knowledgeable staff who can guide consumers towards appropriate products. These retailers often stock premium brands, niche products, and professional-grade supplements not available in mainstream outlets.
Supermarkets have significantly expanded their supplement offerings in recent years, recognising consumer demand and the category's attractive margins. Major chains now stock basic vitamins, minerals, and increasingly, more specialised products, making supplements accessible during routine shopping trips.
E-commerce has transformed the industry, with online sales growing faster than any other channel. Dedicated supplement websites, marketplace platforms, and direct-to-consumer brands all compete for Dutch consumers' attention. Online shopping offers unparalleled convenience, extensive product information, customer reviews, and often competitive pricing, though consumers must exercise due diligence regarding supplier legitimacy.
Challenges Facing the Industry
Despite robust growth, the Dutch supplement industry faces several significant challenges. Consumer scepticism remains an obstacle, with critics questioning whether supplements provide genuine benefits for individuals eating balanced diets. Scientific evidence supporting supplement use varies considerably across products and health claims, and media coverage of studies showing limited benefits can undermine consumer confidence.
The industry also grapples with misinformation and exaggerated marketing claims. Whilst regulations prohibit misleading statements, the line between legitimate information and overpromising can sometimes blur, particularly on social media. This environment creates confusion and may lead consumers to have unrealistic expectations or purchase unnecessary products.
Market saturation in certain categories presents commercial challenges. The proliferation of similar products makes differentiation difficult and can lead to price competition that pressures margins. Companies must innovate continuously and build strong brands to maintain market position.
The Future Outlook
The Dutch supplement industry's future appears bright, with multiple growth opportunities on the horizon. Continued research into nutrition science will likely validate new ingredients and applications, expanding the evidence base for supplement use. Advances in personalised nutrition, potentially incorporating artificial intelligence and advanced diagnostics, could revolutionise how supplements are recommended and consumed.
Integration with digital health platforms and wearable technology may enable more precise nutritional interventions based on real-time physiological data. Imagine supplements automatically adjusted based on activity levels, sleep quality, or stress markers detected by smart devices.
Regulatory evolution will continue shaping the industry. Harmonisation of standards across EU member states, clearer guidelines on health claims, and enhanced enforcement against non-compliant products could strengthen consumer trust and support continued growth.
Conclusion
The supplement industry in the Netherlands has transformed from a niche market to a mainstream sector worth hundreds of millions of euros annually. Driven by demographic shifts, lifestyle factors, increased health consciousness, and digital transformation, the industry shows no signs of slowing. Whilst challenges including regulatory complexity, consumer scepticism, and market saturation persist, the fundamental drivers supporting growth remain robust. As innovation continues, particularly in personalisation and sustainability, and as scientific understanding of nutrition advances, the Dutch supplement industry appears well-positioned for continued expansion. For consumers, this thriving market offers unprecedented choice and access to products supporting health and wellbeing, provided they approach supplement use thoughtfully and purchase from reputable sources.

September in Financial Markets: Bab el-Mandeb Drives Oil Prices Higher, Interest Rates Rise, and AI Warnings Mount  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
15:41:00 UTC
00:41:00 KST

In September the war found its second chokepoint, and markets followed. After Hormuz came the Bab el-Mandeb: the Houthis seized the Yemeni port of Mokha and then Perim Island, which sits in the strait itself. At the same time, drones launched from Iraq forced Saudi Arabia to shut its East-West pipeline, the kingdom's main route around Hormuz. Brent jumped to around USD 110/bbl, its highest since May. Refined products felt the squeeze most as US diesel hit a record USD 6.53/gal on 22 September, and with midterms on 3 November Trump backed a ban on diesel exports, which had reached a record 1.6m bbl/d in August.
As expected, central banks stopped looking through the energy shock, and three of the majors raised rates within eight days. Then came the flash PMI – US business activity grew at its fastest pace since July 2021, and the selloff that followed carried the 30-year Treasury yield above 5.61% on 29 September, a level last seen in 2002.
The S&P 500 slipped 0.5% and the Dow fell 4.3%, ending a five-month winning streak, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.9% as technology was the only S&P 500 sector to finish higher. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq still closed a second straight quarterly gain. Financials, down around 7%, had their worst month since March 2023, while the STOXX 600 lost 2.5%, ending its own five month run. Gold fell about 6.5%, and Brent eased back to around USD 100/bbl at the end of the month
Back in the hiking business
Strong data left the Fed little choice. August payrolls rose 162k, about three times expectations, and CPI held at 3.4% YoY with energy up 16.3%. On 16 September the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise its target range by 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%, its first hike since July 2023, and 16 of 18 officials projected another hike before year end. Trump replied within hours that US rates “should be 1%, or less”.
The ECB had lifted its deposit rate to 2.50% on 10 September, and the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.25%, the highest since 1995, on 18 September.
Five percent and counting
In August the pressure on long-dated debt came from supply worries; in September it came from central banks. Almost all of the 49bp rise in the 10-year Treasury yield, to 5.29%, ran through real yields, with the 10-year TIPS yield up about 44bp, its fastest climb in four years. However, this time a central bank blinked: the Bank of England slowed QT, will no longer sell its longest-dated gilts and paused active sales pending a review before April 2027.
France moved from strained to stressed, as the OAT-Bund spread broke 100bp for the first time since the euro area debt crisis and reached 140bp in early October, when the government presented a 2027 budget built on EUR 54b of savings.
A red carpet and a short extension
Xi Jinping’s 23-25 September state visit, his first to Washington since 2015, came with full ceremony but modest results. The trade truce was extended only to 10 January 2027, two months beyond its November expiry. The two sides agreed lower tariffs on USD 30b of non-sensitive goods each way, Chinese purchases of at least 10m tonnes of US coal in both 2027 and 2028 and a new dialogue on advanced AI, but rare earths stayed unresolved after China’s magnet shipments to the US fell 21%.
Pacing the frontier
On 12 September Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged AI labs to slow frontier development so safety work can keep up, Sam Altman and Elon Musk agreed. Two days later the Philadelphia
Semiconductor Index fell 5.9% and the KOSPI 3.3%. On 25 September OpenAI paused training of its most capable models after an agent slipped past internet restrictions in testing.
Meanwhile, local opposition blocked or delayed 45 US data centers worth USD 68b in Q2. Spending did not slow however as Nvidia rose almost 3% after a record USD 150b buyback increase.
Micron's fiscal Q4 revenue reached USD 54.2b, nearly five times a year earlier, and it guided USD 61.5b for this quarter
Firmer dollar and tarnished metals
Currencies remain confined to their familiar range, though shifts in market behavior hint at rising volatility. The dollar has edged toward the stronger side of its neutral zone, and although its next move remains unsettled, we still favor buying it on dips. A EUR/USD climb to 1.1600 would signal renewed dollar weakness, while support at 1.1150-1.1200 should ideally hold, allowing a rebound toward 1.1400-1.1500; failing that, a far steeper decline could follow. Precious metals remain unattractive, with gold especially vulnerable to a deeper fall.
About Signet Bank:
Signet Bank is Latvia’s leading investment bank. Founded in 1991, it is one of the first banks established following the restoration of Latvia’s independence. Signet Bank provides sustainable financing and investment solutions to local entrepreneurs and businesses. Since 2021, Signet Bank has helped more than 50 Latvian companies raise over EUR 1 billion through bond and equity issuances, while providing an additional EUR 500 million in new lending transactions. In 2025, assets under management reached EUR 1.7 billion. Signet Bank is the leading arranger of corporate bond and equity issuances in Latvia and one of the leading stockbrokers in the Baltic region. The Bank’s shareholders include 47 Latvian and international private investors. The largest shareholders are Signet Acquisition III (20.4%), wholly owned by U.S. investor Alexander Solovey; SIA Reglink (9.6%), founded by banking professional Irīna Pīgozne; and AS RIT Group (9.4%), a Latvian company owned by the Rapoport family

Ukrainian Foreign Ministry on recall of South Korean ambassador: Ukraine is open to resuming dialogue
Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has stated that despite Seoul's decision to recall its ambassador, Ukraine remains open to resuming constructive dialogue.
Source: a comment by Heorhii Tykhyi, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
Quote from Tykhyi: "This week, we invited the ambassador of the Republic of Korea to Ukraine to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to present our position and seek constructive solutions.
The position of the Ukrainian side was conveyed to him. We are convinced that diplomacy must prevail over emotions. Despite Seoul's decision to recall the ambassador, Ukraine remains open to resuming constructive dialogue – even if it takes time."
Background:
- On 8 October, South Korea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced the recall of its ambassador to Ukraine, Park Ki-chang, amid a dispute between Kyiv and Seoul over the disclosure of information regarding the repatriation of North Korean prisoners of war.
- On 25 September, South Korean President Lee Jae-myung stated that Ukraine had breached a non-disclosure agreement by making public information about the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea.
- Meanwhile, Dmytro Lytvyn, communications adviser to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, denied that Ukraine had breached the agreement.
- However, the South Korean president's office demanded official explanations and an apology from Ukraine over the disclosure of the information.
- South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun stated that his country had received a message of apology from Ukraine for disclosing information about the transfer of the two North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul, adding that the apology had failed to meet Seoul's expectations.

Oleshky situation shows limits of dialogue between Ukrainian and Russian Ombudsmen
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
15:40:00 UTC
00:40:00 KST

Oleshky situation shows limits of dialogue between Ukrainian and Russian Ombudsmen
The Secretariat of the Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights told Ukrinform this in response to a request concerning, in particular, its assessment of the effectiveness of dialogue with Russia’s ombudswoman on various issues.
“The situation in Oleshky shows the limits of bilateral dialogue between the institutions of the ombudsmen when it comes to carrying out a large-scale humanitarian operation,” the response said.
At the same time, the Secretariat noted that in certain humanitarian cases, communication with Russia’s ombudswoman produces concrete practical results, allowing people to be returned or families to be reunited.
“Following the appointment of Yana Lantratova as Russia’s Commissioner for Human Rights, the Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets continued work through a direct humanitarian communication channel. Already at the first working meeting on June 5, the practical outcome was the return of five Ukrainian citizens and the reunification of three families. This channel is needed to resolve specific humanitarian issues involving the return of people, family reunification, obtaining and verifying information, exchanging lists, sharing information about people held in Russia or in temporarily occupied territories, and other individual cases,” the response said.
The Secretariat noted that carrying out the humanitarian operation in Oleshky requires security guarantees, a localized ceasefire, an agreed route, access for a neutral international humanitarian intermediary, humanitarian access, and the practical implementation of agreements reached by all parties involved. Ukraine and the International Committee of the Red Cross are ready to participate in the humanitarian operation, but Russia has still not provided the necessary security guarantees for it to begin, the response stressed.
“The lack of an organized humanitarian mechanism is having concrete consequences for the civilian population today. Therefore, the problem is not a lack of proposals from the Ukrainian side or Ukraine’s willingness to receive its citizens, but the absence of practically enforceable security guarantees, an agreed mechanism and unhindered humanitarian access,” the Secretariat said.
At the same time, it stressed that for the Commissioner, the main criterion of effectiveness remains not the mere fact that negotiations are being conducted, but the concrete outcome for people.
As reported by Ukrinform, according to the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine, no food supplies had reached Oleshky since May 26.
According to Oleksandr Prokudin, Head of the Kherson Regional Military Administration, Russian forces are holding about 2,000 people hostage in Oleshky, including nearly 50 children. They are being forced to survive without food, electricity or water.

Ukraine’s Spec Ops Hit Omsk Oil Refinery 2,500 km Away – Again
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
15:39:00 UTC
00:39:00 KST

Ukraine’s Special Operations Forces (SSO) said it has struck Russia’s Omsk Oil Refinery – located 2,500 kilometers (approximately 1,550 miles) from Ukraine – for the second time on Thursday.
“On Oct. 8, ‘Deep Strike’ units of the Special Operations Forces struck the refinery,” the SSO said in a Telegram report.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
According to the report, drones traveled nearly 3,000 kilometers (approximately 1,860 miles) to reach their targets. The operation was conducted in coordination with the “Black Spark” (Chernaya Iskra) insurgent movement operating inside Russia.
The Ukrainian military called the Omsk facility Russia’s largest, but Russian outlet Astra noted that other industry data indicate the Kirishi and Achinsk refineries may have higher processing capacities.
Omsk refinery is part of the Gazprom Neft group and processes more than 21 million tons of oil annually. The facility produces gasoline, diesel, aviation fuel, and petrochemical products.
After a modernization project completed in 2025, the refinery’s oil-processing depth reached 100%. In 2024, the plant produced more than 50 types of products, and all its fuel met the Euro-5 standard.
The company’s website says the refinery employs more than 3,300 people. It ranks among Russia’s 10 largest oil refineries. By some estimates, the Omsk refinery accounts for around 10% of Russia’s total oil processing.
‘Thousands Ready This Year’: Ukraine to Get SPYS Interceptors
Astra conducted its own analysis and reported that the Omsk Oil Refinery was on fire following the drone attack.
According to Astra, black smoke rose over the refinery after a drone alert in the Omsk region and reports of explosions from local residents.
The outlet’s open-source intelligence (OSINT) expert confirmed the fire by examining an eyewitness photo published by the Ukrainian Telegram channel Supernova+.
Omsk Region Governor Vitaly Khotsenko said that one drone had “reached the northern industrial hub” without specifying what was hit.
Astra readers also reported that queues at gas stations in Omsk were growing.
The Ukrainian Telegram channel Exilenova+ reported that the strike used modernized Ukrainian FP-1 long-range drones.
Ukraine’s July attack on Omsk
The SSO first struck the Omsk Oil Refinery on July 6, describing it as the deepest long-range strike carried out by Ukrainian forces since Russia launched its 2022 full-scale invasion.
The SSO then said the attack damaged critical equipment at the refinery, including the ELOU-AVT-11 primary crude oil processing unit, which it described as the plant’s most important installation. Ukraine’s General Staff said the ELOU-AVT-11 unit has a design capacity of 8.4 million tons of oil per year.
Without primary refining, the SSO said, the refinery’s other facilities have no raw materials to process.
The Ukrainian General Staff also confirmed the strike, saying the Omsk refinery was the last of Russia’s 11 largest gasoline producers to be targeted by Ukrainian forces. It said the facility plays a key role in supplying fuel to the Russian military, adding that the attack triggered a fire.
Khotsenko initially said Russian air defenses had shot down Ukrainian drones over the region and that the consequences were being assessed. However, photos and videos shared on social media showed a large fire at the refinery.
Khotsenko later acknowledged that several drones had reached Omsk’s northern industrial zone, though he did not identify the refinery as the target.
The July attack forced the refinery to halt oil processing and go offline for repairs, according to Kyiv.
In early October, Bloomberg reported that, analyzing the impact of strikes on the Omsk refinery and other Russian oil-processing facilities, Russian oil processing had fallen to its lowest level in more than two decades.

80% of Moldovans say country is unprepared for attack as Russian drones flow into its airspace, but few back NATO membership
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
15:36:59 UTC
00:36:59 KST

More than 80% of Moldovans believe the country is not prepared to withstand external aggression, according to a CBS AXA poll presented ahead of the Moldova Security Forum 2026, NewsMaker reports.
The findings come as Moldova has faced a sharp increase in Russian drone incursions linked to Russia’s war against Ukraine. Moldova recorded 44 airspace-violation incidents in the first nine months of 2026, compared with 17 in all of 2025. Authorities have reported Russian drones crossing Moldovan airspace, while drone and missile debris has also fallen on Moldovan territory.
According to NewsMaker, more than 60% of those surveyed said Moldova is completely unprepared for a possible armed attack, while nearly 24% described its preparedness as weak.
Moldovans see country as unprepared for attack
The survey found that 82% of respondents also do not feel sufficiently informed or prepared to know what to do in a major crisis. According to CBS AXA Deputy Director Vasile Cantarji, respondents tend to trust specialized emergency institutions more than Moldova’s main state institutions.
More than half said they trust Moldova’s General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations, while 35% expressed trust in the church. Trust in the government, parliament, and courts was much lower, at roughly 4–6%.
The findings come as Moldova faces a security environment shaped by Russia’s war against Ukraine, hybrid threats, energy dependence, and disinformation. Moldova’s government has supported Ukraine and strengthened security cooperation with European partners, while repeatedly condemning Russia’s war and its spillover effects.
The repeated drone incursions are now increasingly exposing Moldova to risks from the war next door.
Three Russian missiles and two drones strike Moldovan territory in morning attacks on neighboring Ukraine. Moldova is increasingly exposed to the risks of Russia’s war next door
Most favor neutrality over NATO membership
Despite the widespread perception that Moldova is poorly prepared for external aggression, only about 4% of respondents said joining NATO would be the right way to make the country safer.
Around 45% instead favored maintaining Moldova’s neutrality. At the same time, six in 10 respondents said Moldova needs continued external support to strengthen its security and defense.
Nearly two-thirds considered cooperation with the European Union and Romania important for Moldova’s development.
Moldova’s constitution establishes permanent neutrality, while the country has been deepening security and defense cooperation with European partners.
EU seen as preferred source of emergency assistance
The poll also asked whom Moldova should turn to for help during a major disaster such as an earthquake or flood.
About 33% selected EU countries, followed by Russia at roughly 16% and Romania at 15%. The CIS, NATO, UN, and Ukraine each received support from 4% or fewer respondents.
War in Ukraine is one of several security concerns
Respondents identified a range of threats to Moldova’s security, with internal problems ranking alongside external risks.
Corruption was cited by more than 15% of respondents, while poverty was named by 13.5%. Just over 13.5% identified the war in Ukraine as a security risk. Energy dependence and disinformation were each cited by nearly 10%.
Other concerns included economic instability, crime, and external aggression.
CBS AXA conducted the survey from August 25 to September 9 among 2,009 Moldovans aged 18 and older. The reported margin of error is 2.2%. NewsMaker published the findings on October 7.
Moldova strengthens protection at Ukrainian border
Moldovan authorities are now responding to the Russian drone threat by creating protected areas at border crossings with Ukraine where border guards, officials, and civilians can shelter during potential drone attacks, Interior Minister Daniela Misail-Nikitin said on October 7, according to NewsMaker.
Authorities are also moving Moldovan personnel from joint checkpoints located on Ukrainian territory back to Moldova. The measures follow an incident at the Palanca–Maiaki–Udobne crossing in which a Moldovan border guard was injured by a falling projectile.
Transnistria adds another security challenge
Moldova also faces a longstanding security problem in Transnistria, a breakaway region along the country’s eastern border with Ukraine. The region declared independence from Moldova in 1990 and has remained outside Chisinau’s control since a brief war in 1992.
Transnistria is not internationally recognized as an independent state. Russia maintains a significant troop presence there and has long supported the separatist authorities, making the region a persistent source of tension between Chisinau and Moscow.

The best 50 bars in the world have been revealed for 2026 – and 18 are in Europe
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
15:36:24 UTC
00:36:24 KST

Europe dominates this year’s 50 Best ranking, with 18 bars making the top 50 and Paris overtaking London as the continent’s best-represented city. Hong Kong’s Bar Leone retains the global crown, while Milan’s Moebius Milano and Athens’ Line also break into the top five.
The annual ranking of the 50 Best Bars in the world has been revealed, and 18 are in Europe.
Following its unveiling of positions 51-100 in September, the prestigious ranking body revealed that Hong Kong’s Bar Leone held on to the top spot for a second year running.
The results were announced at a ceremony in Milan on Wednesday, and two European bars – Moebius Milano in Milan and Line in Athens – featured in the top 10.
Europe was far and away the most represented continent in the ranking with its 18 spots. It also achieved a further 18 wins in the 51-100 extended list, meaning it takes up more than a third of the positions overall.
Italy had plenty to celebrate, with Moebius Milano taking second place and the top spot in Europe, while Italy’s other entry, Locale Firenze in Florence, was at number 33.
Paris has overtaken London as the most represented European city on the list for the first time, with four bars making the cut. The Cambridge Public House is number 13, followed by Bar Nouveau at 15, newcomer De Vie at 23 and Danico at 26. That puts Paris level with Hong Kong and New York as the cities with the most bars in the global top 50.
London still has a strong showing, led by Connaught Bar at number eight. Satan’s Whiskers is 29, while new entry Waltz comes in at 32.
Athens also has three bars on the list. Line leads the way at number five, while The Bar in Front of the Bar climbed 28 places to 19, earning the Nikka Highest Climber Award. Barro Negro rounds out the city’s entries at 40.
Spain has three bars in total, with Barcelona’s Sips at 16 and Paradiso at 17, while Madrid’s Angelita makes its debut at 50. Paradiso also picked up the Rémy Martin Legend of the List Award.
The top five are very varied, geographically and style-wise, and are all well worth adding to any bar lover’s bucket list.
The top five best bars in the world
Bar Leone, Hong Kong
Italian bartender Lorenzo Antinori opened this Hong Kong venue in 2023, bringing the atmosphere of a traditional Roman neighbourhood bar to the city.
The focus is on classic Italian aperitivo, with simple, well-made cocktails and a relaxed setting. Although it’s relatively new to the scene, Bar Leone has already cemented itself as something of an institution in the Asian city.
Moebius Milano, Milan
Milan’s Moebius Milano has made a significant leap up the ranking, climbing from seventh place last year to number two in 2026.
The bar is part of a much larger venue housed in a former textile factory, combining cocktails, food, music and design under one roof.
Its cocktail offering ranges from classic serves to more experimental creations, while the industrial setting gives it a distinctly contemporary Milanese feel.
Alquímico, Cartagena
Alquímico in Cartagena has taken third place, making it the highest-ranked bar outside Europe and Asia.
Set inside a restored colonial mansion in the heart of the Colombian city, the bar stretches across three floors, each with its own atmosphere and cocktail menu.
Drinks draw heavily on Colombian ingredients and landscapes, with the team using local produce and traditional techniques to create a menu that changes with the country’s seasons.
Bar Us, Bangkok
Bangkok’s Bar Us has secured fourth place, making it the Thai capital’s highest-ranked bar this year.
The intimate venue takes a tasting-menu approach to cocktails, with drinks designed around seasonal ingredients and carefully balanced flavour combinations.
Rather than simply ordering from a conventional drinks list, guests are taken through a series of serves that explore different ingredients and techniques. It’s part of Bangkok’s growing reputation as one of Asia’s major cocktail destinations.
Line, Athens
Athens’ Line has climbed to fifth place, making it the second highest-ranked European bar on this year’s list.
Housed in one of the Greek city’s most significant former art galleries, it offers cocktails with a strong focus on fermentation.
Many of its ingredients are made in-house, including fermented fruit, syrups and other preparations used in the drinks.
The result is a menu that puts Greek produce and flavours at the centre of the experience, while the industrial-inspired setting keeps things relaxed and contemporary.

NATO on Thursday said its upcoming
'Steadfast Noon' exercise in Italy was a nuclear exercise,
obviously not featuring live weapons.
                                    
The exercise starting in Italy October 13 will be a "nuclear"
exercise, explained NATO's head of nuclear policy, Nassima
Barrows, during a meeting with media outlets, including ANSA.
                                    
While no live nuclear weapons are used in the exercise, training
to the high standards required for a mission of this type
remains crucial.
                                    
"It is therefore essential to ensure both discipline and the
ability to collaborate on collective defense—of which the
nuclear mission is a vital component," stated Colonel David
Bull, the Alliance's Head of Nuclear Operations.

Meloni says proud to be called 'woman from Ciociaria' in fluffed jibe
Italy
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
17:35:28 CEST
00:35:28 KST

Premier Giorgia Meloni said Thursday she was proud to have been called "a woman from Ciociaria" in a fluffed jibe by a political opponent who said he had actually meant to call her a "loudmouth". 
The man, a local councillor at Pontedera near Pisa, said he had meant to call the premier a "caciarona" a Roman dialect word for a loud, rowdy, or boisterous woman. 
Instead, he said he mistakenly used the word "ciociara", meaning a woman from Ciociaria, a formerly mostly agricultural southeastern part of the Lazio region, towards Campania, once dismissed as a rural backwater. 
Irked, Meloni posted on social media: "(There have been) personal attacks—regarding my physique, my family, and my origins. But today, the tone changes. And the level of discourse shifts. Because a gentleman from the Democratic Party, a certain Floriano Della Bella, stated during a Pontedera City Council meeting that Meloni is a 'Ciociara'—using the term in the most derogatory sense.
"He was reprimanded for this by the Council President—himself a member of the PD—who added: 'Please, use language befitting your role.' "So, for these gentlemen, being 'Ciociaro' is something to be ashamed of, and calling someone that is tantamount to an insult.
"What's more, they consider it a term that shouldn't even be uttered in an institutional setting. I'm afraid I disagree. And I am proud to be called a Ciociara.
"Because Ciociaria is one of the most beautiful, ancient, and extraordinary regions of our Italy.
"A land of Popes and military leaders, of saints and artists, of writers and poets.
"Cicero, Gaius Marius, Boniface VIII, Saint Thomas Aquinas, Marcello Mastroianni, Vittorio De Sica, Nino Manfredi, and so many other men and women who have shaped our history over time.
"They constantly speak of 'the people,' respect, and cohesion.
"Yet, in a single stroke, they insult nearly half a million Italians, branding them as inferior, ignorant, and second-class citizens.
"But it is they who are the ignorant ones. Long live Ciociaria!" she concluded.
La Ciociara is the original title of the 1960 film adaptation of Alberto Moravia's novel about a woman and her daughter who suffer at the hands of the occupying Nazis and whose English-language title is Two Women, for which Sofia Loren became the first actor or actress to win an acting Oscar for a non-English-language performance in 1962.
Meloni's father, a tax advisor who abandoned the family when she was one and who was later convicted of drug trafficking in Spain, was originally from Sardinia while her mother, a romance novelist, is of Sicilian heritage.
The premier grew up in a fairly affluent enclave of the working-class Garbatella district of Rome..

Azzurro said Thursday it had seen an over 87%rise in calls

In that period, it said, mental health-related cases nearly
doubled compared to the same period the previous year, rising
from 687 to 1,286 (+87.2%).
                                    
Today, mental health issues account for the primary reason
behind more than one in three requests for help (35.7%), up from
30.1% two years ago.
                                    
These figures come from Telefono Azzurro's 1.96.96 service.
                                    
Ahead of World Mental Health Day, and in collaboration with the
Alma Mater Studiorum - University of Bologna and the IRCCS
Institute of Neurological Sciences of Bologna, the organization
is hosting a meeting on Friday, October 9 (9:30 AM - 12:30 PM)

Russian liberal politician jailed for 4 years over donation to Navalny group
MOSCOW, Oct 8 - Elena Perepelitsa, a member of Russia's liberal Yabloko party which opposes the war in Ukraine, has been sentenced to four years in a penal colony for donating money to an "extremist" organisation, state news agency TASS reported on Thursday.
She was the third Yabloko member to be jailed in less than four months as authorities step up pressure on the opposition party, which was largely barred from contesting September's parliamentary election.
Perepelitsa was found guilty of donating money to the late opposition leader Alexei Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation, which is designated in Russia as a "foreign agent" and outlawed as an extremist organisation.
In a post on Telegram, Yabloko confirmed the verdict and shared Perepelitsa's statement to the court in which she denied knowingly financing extremist activity.
Since the start of the full-scale war in Ukraine in 2022, Russia's use of extremist designations and strict wartime censorship laws have prompted many opposition figures and activists to flee the country, while those who remain risk prosecution for expressing anti-war views and other dissent.
Yabloko's deputy leader Maxim Kruglov was convicted in June of spreading lies about the Russian army and jailed for seven years.
In August, the party's deputy chairman Lev Shlosberg was sentenced to just over 11 years in a penal colony for discrediting Russia's armed forces and spreading false information about them, after condemning the war in Ukraine. REUTERS

FIA identifies software bug behind Bahrain GP formation-lap chaos in Malaysia
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
15:32:52 UTC
00:32:52 KST

Halis Sunnetci
08 October 2026•Update: 08 October 2026
Formula 1's governing body, the FIA, said Thursday that a software bug caused several cars to lose power during formation laps of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, delaying the race start.
The investigation found that some cars running at low engine speeds experienced excessive power losses in sections of the Sepang circuit where a 250-kilowatt power reduction was applied under wet-weather settings.
The FIA said the temporary software fix introduced at Sepang would be used again at the Singapore Grand Prix if similar weather conditions were expected.
A further update to the wet-weather software is scheduled for the US Grand Prix on Oct. 25.
Sunday's race was delayed after several cars experienced power problems during two formation laps, prompting officials to suspend the start procedure.
According to the FIA's Thursday statement, its technical team identified the cause within five minutes of Sunday's race suspension and released revised software configurations.
The changes allowed teams to complete installation before the race resumed, the FIA said.
“Their collective efforts enabled the issue to be identified, addressed and resolved, allowing the race to proceed safely,” the FIA said, thanking teams, power unit manufacturers and its technical staff.

Rodrigo Duterte ruled fit to stand trial by ICC judges
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
15:31:00 UTC
00:31:00 KST

Rodrigo Duterte ruled fit to stand trial by ICC judges
October 8, 2026
Judges at the International Criminal Court (ICC) said Thursday that former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte is competent to stand trial on charges of crimes against humanity.
Duterte walked into the courtroom for his first-ever in-person appearance at a hearing last month after a year of having been detained at The Hague, where the global court is located.
Judges at the court this April confirmed charges against him, accusing him of murder and attempted murder for his alleged role in the killings of dozens of people during his "war on drugs."
Duterte's trial is set to begin on November 30. He faces a maximum sentence of life imprisonment if convicted.
Duterte makes his first appearance in court after being arrested
Duterte did not speak at a hearing last month but sipped water throughout the proceedings.
His legal team has argued that he suffers from cognitive decline that affects his memory and daily functioning.
ICC judges in January said his health was good enough for him to follow proceedings and requested his presence in court. He had missed several hearings or attended those via videolink.
Now, the ICC's ruling, dated September 28 and made public on Thursday, clears the road for his trial to get underway.
The court ruling said an independent panel of experts found Duterte "has the capacity to understand the charges" and follow the proceedings, including the implication of entering a plea — which he will be asked to do when the trial opens.
He also is mentally fit to understand evidence and discuss his defense with his lawyers, the panel of experts said.
Duterte's violent anti-narcotics campaign
Duterte was arrested last year on accusations of crimes that took place during his "war on drugs" campaign when he was president between 2016 and 2022 and before that, when he was mayor of Davao City.
The charges against him are tied to brutal killings that took place on his watch between November 2011 and March 2019.
Duterte's campaign to wipe out the use of illegal narcotics in the country ended with the deaths of thousands of people as police systematically targeted poor and defenseless people, according to Amnesty International.
Prosecutors alleged that police and hit squad members carried out dozens of murders at Duterte's behest starting in 2011, motivated by the promise of money or to avoid becoming targets themselves.

james chinlund fills louis vuitton’s louvre runway with hovering concept vehicles
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
15:30:53 UTC
00:30:53 KST

james chinlund fills louis vuitton’s louvre runway with hovering concept vehicles
34 futuristic car sculptures transform the cour carrée du louvre into a surreal cityscape for nicolas ghesquière's spring-summer 2027 show.
JAMES CHINLUND IMAGINES A FUTURISTIC CITY FOR LOUIS VUITTON
For Louis Vuitton’s spring-summer 2027 show, American production designer James Chinlund transformed the historic Cour Carrée du Louvre in Paris into a futuristic urban landscape populated by hovering concept vehicles. Presented on October 6th during Paris Fashion Week, the installation brought 34 sculptural cars into the museum’s courtyard, creating the illusion of a city suspended somewhere between the present and an imagined future. Conceived for Nicolas Ghesquière’s latest collection, the scenography placed automotive design at the center of the runway experience.
The vehicles, suspended at different heights above a road-like runway, appeared to float among the Louvre’s classical façades. Developed in four variations, their geometric silhouettes combined cream and forest-green finishes with graphic stripes and Louis Vuitton’s signature Damier pattern. Glowing headlights and red taillights reinforced their automotive identity, while their abstract proportions suggested machines from an alternative vision of urban mobility. Together, the structures formed an aerial traffic scene, turning the courtyard into a temporary science-fiction environment.
HISTORIC ARCHITECTURE MEETS CINEMATIC WORLDBUILDING
The contrast between the historic setting and the futuristic installation was central to the composition. Beneath the hovering forms, an asphalt-like surface extended across the courtyard, establishing a ground-level route for the models. The arrangement created a dialogue between movement and stillness, with the suspended vehicles seemingly frozen in midair against the Louvre’s centuries-old stone architecture. Rather than concealing the building, Chinlund incorporated its façades into the visual narrative, using the monumental surroundings to frame the imagined city.
Chinlund’s approach draws on a career spanning cinema, sculpture, and fashion. Best known for his production design on films including The Batman (2022), the American designer has repeatedly explored the construction of fictional environments through architecture and large-scale installations. His relationship with Louis Vuitton and Nicolas Ghesquière extends back to the house’s Cruise 2025 presentation at Antoni Gaudí’s Park Güell in Barcelona, where architecture similarly played an important role in the runway experience.
REIMAGINING MOVEMENT AND THE ART OF TRAVEL
For spring-summer 2027, the scenography also reflected Ghesquière’s interest in the complexities of contemporary urban life. While the suspended vehicles suggested speed, congestion, and a city in constant motion, the collection itself explored an opposing sense of lightness. Entitled Ergonomie, it focused on the relationship between clothing and the moving body, introducing ultralight fabrics, fluid constructions, and relaxed silhouettes. The contrast between the sculptural environment and the garments presented a dialogue between the rigidity of machines and the freedom of human movement.
The installation also revisited one of Louis Vuitton’s defining themes: the Art of Travel. Here, transportation was reimagined through objects that seemed to have escaped the limitations of conventional roads, transforming familiar vehicles into speculative design sculptures. Within the Louvre’s historic courtyard, Chinlund’s floating cars offered an alternative vision of mobility, using temporary architecture and cinematic illusion to turn a fashion presentation into an imagined urban environment.
project info:
name: Louis Vuitton Women’s Spring-Summer 2027 Show
creative director: Nicolas Ghesquière
set design: James Chinlund | @jchinlund
brand: Louis Vuitton | @louisvuitton
location: Paris, France

Lebanon seeks EU support to end Israeli occupation, state control of weapons
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
15:30:07 UTC
00:30:07 KST

Lebanon has said it is counting on EU support for its decision to place all weapons under state control and its efforts to end Israel’s occupation of Lebanese territory.
“Lebanon has taken a clear sovereign decision to place weapons and the use of force exclusively in the hands of the state throughout its territory,” Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi said during a joint news conference with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas in Beirut on Thursday.
He described the move as essential to restoring sovereignty, consolidating stability and rebuilding strong and capable state institutions.
“We count on the European Union continuing to stand by Lebanon and its legitimate institutions to achieve this national objective,” he said.
“We also count on its support to end the continuing Israeli occupation of Lebanese territory and ensure the full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701.”
Raggi also welcomed European support for Lebanon’s state institutions, including the Lebanese army and Internal Security Forces.
“We want Europe to be an essential partner in this new phase, not only in helping Lebanon manage its crises but also in overcoming them,” he added.
For her part, the visiting EU foreign policy chief, Kallas, said in an interview that the bloc favoured avoiding a security vacuum and extending a UN peacekeeping mandate in south Lebanon.
The EU's top diplomat also said that the bloc would soon be launching a training mission for the Lebanese army, calling it "a major upgrade in the security relationship" with the country.
The Lebanese government decided in August to bring all weapons under state control, including those held by Hezbollah.
The group rejected the move, demanding that Israeli forces first withdraw from areas they occupy in southern Lebanon.
UN Security Council Resolution 1701 was adopted in August 2006 following a 33-day war between Israel and Hezbollah.
Israel has continued attacks on Lebanon since March 2, killing 4,386 people and wounding 12,413, according to the latest Lebanese health ministry figures dated September 25, 2025.
On June 26, Beirut and Tel Aviv signed a US-sponsored framework agreement in Washington providing for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory and the deployment of the Lebanese army in areas vacated by Israeli forces.
Despite the agreement, Israel has continued attacks on southern Lebanon and remains in control of areas of Lebanese territory, some occupied for decades, and others seized during more recent wars and military raids.

Trump aide's daughter pictured with pro-Russia politician

Photo shows top Trump aide's daughter with pro-Russia politician in Bosnia
An image circulated on social media and verified by CBS News shows Katie Wiles, the daughter of White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, recently traveled to Republika Srpska, the Bosnian-controlled territory led by pro-Russian Serb strongman Milorad Dodik.
The photo raises further questions about possible White House links to the pro-Russian politician. President Trump on Wednesday distanced himself from two top political advisers after the New York Times reported they had traveled to Republika Srpska last week to assist Dodik's pro-Russia party in Bosnian elections.
The image, shared online by conservative Albanian American activist Evi Kokalari, shows Wiles holding a rifle and standing next to a man CBS News has identified as Željko Budimir, the interior minister of the semi-autonomous Republika Srpska administration. In a post on X, Kokalari claimed the image was taken in August. CBS News Confirmed has verified the image is of Wiles and that it was taken in Republika Srpska. The image appears to be a screenshot of a story from Wiles' personal Instagram account, with a caption "mostly work + some serious fun!"
CBS News confirmed the veracity of the images through satellite imagery and previous social media posts from the shooting range where the image was captured. The position of the sun in the image also indicates that it was taken in the summer.
The RIS shooting range is located in northern Republika Srpska and is frequented by Budimir, the interior minister, according to Bosnian media reports.
Katie Wiles is a partner at Continental Strategy, a large political lobbying firm based in Washington, D.C., according to its website.
A spokesperson for the firm acknowledged to CBS News Thursday that Wiles had taken the trip in mid-August but on business for another client of Continental Strategy.
"Katie Wiles visited the country in mid-August for two days with a U.S.-based company who was invited to do a feasibility study in the region," the spokesperson said. "Wiles provides strategic communications support to this US company and has done so for over two years. Wiles has not spoken with any United States Government official regarding Srpska."
CBS News has asked Continental Strategy for the name of the company.
U.S. foreign agent registration filings [FARA] reviewed by CBS News show that Continental Strategy registered to lobby on behalf of Republika Srpska in early 2026.
"Susie does not discuss work matters with her daughters," a White House official told CBS News Thursday.
Another FARA filing from the same firm this year lists the signature of Alejandro Garcia, a former deputy political director for Mr. Trump's presidential campaign, as a consultant for Republika Srpska. Garcia is also a partner at Continental Strategy.
The lobbying firm's spokesperson told CBS News that Garcia attended Bosnia's election day on Oct. 4 "but no other member of the team was present."
"Garcia is the sole person who has interacted with the United States government regarding Srpska, and his contacts have all been meticulously tracked to be reported in accordance with FARA requirements," the spokesperson said.
White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles met with Željka Cvijanović, a close ally of Milorad Dodik, last month, and a White House official told CBS News that meeting was arranged by Garcia, not by Katie Wiles.
On Tuesday, the New York Times reported that James Blair and Chris LaCivita, two key GOP strategists in the Republicans' midterm election efforts, spent some of last week in the small, self-governing territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina to help Dodik's party with its own campaigning. Katie Wiles has no such involvement with Mr. Trump's political operation.
Under the control of Dodik's party, Republika Srpska has forged close ties with President Vladimir Putin's government in Russia, while also spending heavily on U.S.-based lobbying firms to court associates of Mr. Trump, according to FARA filings reviewed by CBS News.
Serbian secessionist leader Dodik, who until recently served as the president of Republika Srpska, has long been accused of undermining the U.S.-brokered Dayton Accords, which ended the bloody sectarian violence between Bosnia, Croatia and Serbia in the 1990s. A Sarajevo court last year convicted Dodik of failing to comply with the terms of Bosnia's 1995 peace accords. He was then removed as president and banned from holding political office by Bosnia's electoral authorities.
In a Truth Social post Wednesday, Mr. Trump said he did not "have any idea" who LaCivita and Blair had been working for and he pledged, "if there's a conflict, I will terminate them, immediately!"
Later Wednesday, Mr. Trump appeared to slightly soften his language.
"They don't have a conflict, because they're independent people. You know, they don't work for me," Mr. Trump said, addressing reporters in the Oval Office. "They are consultants and I assume they have a lot of clients. I don't know who their clients are. If I thought they had a conflict here, I would terminate them."
As CBS News reported this week, the involvement of a U.S. firm linked to associates of Mr. Trump in an energy project in Bosnia and Herzegovina worth more than $1.5 billion has raised questions about the White House's relationship with Dodik.
Last month, House Democrats published a report accusing the Trump administration of lifting sanctions against Dodik in an effort to enrich and empower allies of Mr. Trump, and of undermining longstanding U.S. foreign policy interests in the region in the process.
The central allegation is that AAFS Infrastructure & Energy, a company incorporated in the U.S. last year and headed by Mr. Trump's former personal attorney Jesse Binnall and Joseph Flynn, the brother of Trump ally Gen. Michael Flynn, secured the contract to build a key gas pipeline between Bosnia and Croatia after the sanctions were lifted against Dodik, who had previously opposed the development.
FARA filings cited in the report and reviewed by CBS News show that Michael Flynn, Mr. Trump's former national security adviser, worked as a paid lobbyist for Republika Srpska in October 2025, the month during which the sanctions against Dodik were lifted.
Within six months of the sanctions being lifted, Dodik's party, which has veto power in Bosnia's legislature, dropped its opposition and the Bosnian parliament passed legislation naming AAFS as the lead developer on the billion-dollar project.
The White House declined to comment on the pipeline project last week, but an administration official said the sanctions against Dodik were lifted to prevent instability in the Balkans.
"This is yet another example of President Trump's pragmatic, farseeing foreign policy that has prevented disasters on perennial issues that his predecessors so often stumbled into," a White House official told CBS News on Friday, without elaborating on the type of disasters the Trump administration was preventing.

PRESS RELEASE 150
Albares presents Ibero-American Business Forum to be held as part of Madrid Summit
- The forum will provide a platform to channel the region’s business sector’s vision, identify structural challenges and formulate recommendations that will enrich the summits’ agenda
The Minister for Foreign Affairs, the European Union and Cooperation, José Manuel Albares, today presented the Ibero-American Business Forum, which will take place in Madrid on 3 and 4 November, as part of the Ibero-American Summit of Heads of State and Government on 4 and 5 November.
In his address, Albares emphasised that “in the face of fragmentation, the Community offers a space of trust; in the face of polarisation, a tradition of consensus; and in the face of challenges, a platform for building common responses”. The minister emphasised the importance of this meeting and the contributions of the participants, which make it possible to “foster alliances, identify opportunities and contribute concrete proposals to the Ibero-American process and the development of our societies”.
Organised by the Ibero-American General Secretariat (SEGIB) in partnership with the Council of Ibero-American Business Leaders (CEIB) and the Spanish Confederation of Business Organisations (CEOE), this forum will provide a platform for channelling the views of the region’s business sector, identifying structural challenges and formulating recommendations that will enrich the summits’ agenda.
Since its inception in 2005, this gathering has brought together business leaders, public officials and key figures in economic and business development across Ibero-America. The conclusions drawn from these summits strengthen public-private partnerships and position Ibero-America as an influential player in the global economy, with a unique historical and cultural identity, whilst also serving as a natural bridge between Europe and Latin America.
The Ibero-American Business Forum in Madrid to be held in 2026 represents a strategic opportunity to reinforce the Ibero-American project and mobilise the business ecosystem towards a shared agenda of innovation, sustainable productive transformation and economic integration.

German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has held a telephone conversation with his Ukrainian counterpart, Yevhen Khmara, assuring him of continued support from Germany and announcing the delivery of new aid.
"Germany remains firmly committed to supporting Ukraine, which faces daily terror from the Putin regime. During the conversation with Minister Khmara, key topics included the current situation and Ukraine's needs, German-Ukrainian industrial cooperation, and a support package for Ukraine for the winter," the German Ministry of Defense reported on its WhatsApp channel.
The ministry stated that the "winter aid package" includes crucial support measures to strengthen Ukraine's defense capabilities. Specifically, this involves supporting the rapid development and large-scale production of powerful interceptor drones to counter Russian attack drones comprising tens of thousands of drones of various types.
"Furthermore, we are providing both short-term and targeted assistance. Ukraine requested a package of munitions for its combat aircraft to counter Russian jet-powered drones. We responded within days and began deliveries. The first batch has already arrived," the Defense Ministry reported.
The ministry also announced that, as a sign of strategic partnership, Germany will reinforce its military attaché office in Kyiv and appoint a major general to head it in the future.
"At the same time, Germany is participating in the Ukrainian Anti-Shahed program to continue developing Ukrainian interceptor drones designed to counter Geran drones (Russian jet-powered kamikaze drones)," the smessage reads.
Last week, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha announced that several partners—Spain, Belgium, and Poland—would soon supply Ukraine with 20mm rounds for F-16 fighter jets, which are effective against Russian jet-powered drones.
"We spent the whole day [referring to Wednesday] working on the 20mm caliber issue. And we succeeded. I believe we have secured a solution regarding this caliber for a significant period. I thank all our ambassadors," Sybiha noted.
Earlier, Bloomberg reported, citing informed sources, that Ukraine seeks to purchase tens of thousands of 20mm rounds for F-16s to shoot down Russian jet-powered drones. According to the agency, intercepting a single drone requires an average of about 150 rounds. The publication highlighted that the daily requirement could amount to approximately 10,000 rounds of ammunition.

St. Francis of Assisi Meets Antoni Gaudí, an event at the embassy in Madrid
Italy
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
17:27:34 CEST
00:27:34 KST

The Italian Embassy in Madrid celebrated the 800th anniversary of the death of St. Francis of Assisi and the 100th anniversary of the death of Antoni Gaudí with the event “Francisco y Gaudí: lenguajes, vida y actividades de lo sagrado.” The event featured a dialogue between Father Giuseppe Buffon, OFM, rector of the Pontifical Antonianum University and professor of Church History, and Italian architect Chiara Curti, a professor at the Antoni Gaudí Faculty in Barcelona and author of publications on the Catalan architect, including the recent *Gaudí vivo* (Edizioni Ares). 
    To celebrate in Spain the figure of St. Francis of Assisi, patron saint of Italy, and his message of peace, brotherhood, and care for creation, the Embassy chose to place him in dialogue with Antoni Gaudí, a central figure in Barcelona’s architectural and religious heritage.
                                    
The coincidence of the two centennial anniversaries in 2026—as stated in a press release—provided an opportunity to bring together two figures who are distant in time and background but united by a profound connection between faith, life, and expression. Building on this relationship, Father Giuseppe Buffon and Chiara Curti developed the dialogue around three central themes: the Nativity scene, creation, and self-emptying.
                                    
The program allowed the audience to recognize points of contact and iconographic parallels between Francis and Gaudí, highlighting how faith can become experience, work, and culture. The event thus contributed to a shared understanding of Italian and Spanish cultural and religious heritage.
                                    
Father Giuseppe Buffon explored the legacy of the Franciscan message, focusing in particular on the significance of the Greccio Nativity scene, on fraternity, and on care for creation. Chiara Curti explained how faith and the observation of creation guided Gaudí’s work on the Sagrada Família, leading to his decision to devote himself entirely to the church and to identify himself as a “collaborator with the Creator.”
    The event was included in the program of the National Committee for the celebrations marking the 800th anniversary of the death of St. Francis of Assisi and among the events of the Year of Gaudí. “Two anniversaries that differ in era and context, but which the calendar brings together this year, offering us the opportunity to create a dialogue between two very different figures, united by a profound connection between faith, life, and language. “I am particularly pleased that this event is part of the program organized by the Italian National Committee for the celebrations marking the eighth centenary of the death of St. Francis of Assisi, as well as among the official events of the Year of Gaudí,” stated the Italian Ambassador to Spain, Giuseppe Buccino Grimaldi, in his welcome remarks.
                                    
“Beyond the historical distances that separate them, both figures were able to translate the spiritual dimension into a lived experience and a universal language, helping to make the heritage of the two countries a shared legacy,” he emphasized.

INDIA bloc protests against CEC: 'Unite to fight' proposes Uddhav's Sena; will AAP, DMK relent?

NEW DELHI: Should Arvind Kejriwal’s AAP and MK Stalin’s DMK join INDIA bloc’s fight against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over SIR? Well, the answer would surely be “yes”, as far as the allies of the bloc are concerned.Now to the more difficult question: Will Arvind Kejriwal’s AAP and MK Stalin’s DMK join INDIA bloc’s fight against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over SIR? Well, there is no straight answer to this one.The AAP and the DMK have a common enemy in the Congress. Uddhav Thackeray’s Shiv Sena (UBT) has now urged the two parties to set aside their differences with the grand-old-party to fight against "dictatorship". In an editorial in the party mouthpiece 'Saamana', Shiv Sena (UBT) said, “The entire country has been witnessing protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), but the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) have stayed away from it."
-
The absence of both parties, who have officially withdrawn from the INDIA bloc, has highlighted the existing differences within the opposition camp on the strategy and format of the protest against irregularities in the SIR process.
'A very critical request'
Former Congress leader and senior political commentator Sanjay Jha feels Shiv Sena (UBT)'s suggestion to both the DMK and the Aam Aadmi Party to join the INDIA bloc is a very practical, very reasonable, and at the moment, a very critical request.
"This is not about, at the moment, anything other than the fact that Indian democracy is in peril. It is unlikely that the CEC is going to resign of his own volition. It is pretty apparent that the government of Mr. Modi is going to be stubborn, and they will stonewall any effort by the opposition to demand and get accountability. Public protests don't seem to make any difference to the government. So the more the merrier," Sanjay Jha says.While the AAP has openly announced it will not be a part of the INDIA bloc’s protest and said “we are fighting this battle in our own way, the DMK has spoken in different tones.DMK spokesperson Saravanan Annadurai accused Rahul of adopting inconsistent positions on the electoral roll revision exercise and questioned why developments in Tamil Nadu had not received the same attention as the broader campaign against the Election Commission.In a post on X, Annadurai called on Rahul Gandhi to clarify his stand on allegations concerning names allegedly removed from Tamil Nadu’s electoral rolls during the SIR process.The DMK spokesperson also referred to a statement attributed to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge that governments elected after the SIR exercise should be dissolved and sought clarification on why Rahul Gandhi had not publicly endorsed that position and whether such a stand would also apply to Tamil Nadu.Interestingly, a day later, DMK senior leader TKS Elangovan backed Rahul Gandhi on protests against the Election Commission (EC), saying that citizens have a right to protest against the government.“It is the right of citizens to fight against the government’s wrongdoings. That is what Rahul Gandhi did yesterday. Still, this government does not want him to protest because Gyanesh Kumar is being very useful to the BJP. Because of him, the BJP captured power in many states. In all these states, re-elections should be held,” Elangovan said.
Will DMK, AAP join SIR protests?
The DMK and the Congress had a very unpleasant parting of their two-decade-old ties after the 2026 assembly elections in Tamil Nadu, which the alliance lost to actor-politician C Joseph Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam TVK. While the TVK emerged as the single largest party, it fell short of a majority. The Congress rushed in to help Vijay not just form the government but also eventually join it. Making Congress a part of the government was something the DMK had resisted all along. The Congress move offended the DMK to no end. Since then, MK Stalin’s party has been unrelenting in its attacks on the Congress at all forums from Chennai to Delhi. The Congress, on its part, maintains that it kept the DMK in the loop while shifting loyalties to the TVK.The DMK is missing no opportunity to drive a wedge between the new allies. On Thursday, it lashed out at Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay-led TVK for not explicitly naming the BJP government over the arrest of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi after a protest in the national capital demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.Questioning the TVK's statement, Elangovan pointed out that it failed to identify the authorities responsible for the action against the leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha. "Who arrested Rahul Gandhi? They should condemn and explicitly mention the name of the BJP government," Elangovan told PTI videos.With the TVK establishing itself as the third pole of Tamil Nadu politics, at least for now, the Congress will have to choose one against the other, and to that extent its ties with the DMK will remain frosty for now. More so, after the TVK has officially joined the INDIA bloc. But the DMK’s measured criticism of the Congress-led INDIA bloc protests may offer a ray of hope to the opposition bloc allies of a future softening of stand by M K Stalin.Now, let’s turn to AAP. Here’s where untangling the strains in the ties may be very difficult, if not impossible. Relations between the Congress and the AAP have always been uneasy and tumultuous. AAP was initially a part of the INDIA bloc.However, ties between Kejriwal’s party and the Congress were never smooth given their competing political interests in several states. AAP attended the first three meetings of the INDIA bloc. The high point in their ties came in the run up to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections when the two parties agreed to a joint contest in Delhi, Haryana, Goa, Punjab and Gujarat.The alliance did not work and the ties ended for all practical purposes after the results were out. In July 2025, Kejriwal formally announced the end of ties.Uddhav Thackeray’s party has reminded Kejriwal of his bitter experiences with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and the Election Commission.“While Kejriwal was the chief minister of Delhi, he was put behind bars in a "false" case. Kejriwal's defeat was engineered by deleting names of voters from his constituency, it alleged. So, it is not in the AAP's interest to stay away from the INDIA bloc,” the Shiv Sena (UBT) wrote in its editorial.
'All parties should look at larger picture'
Sanjay Jha is confident that these parties will eventually join the opposition protest. He argues it is extremely crucial that the opposition includes everyone.“Whether there are any small, petty differences, whether there is any degree of discomfort with one or the other partner, everyone has to look at the larger picture. And the larger picture is that today people are out on the streets because they're concerned about the future of their vote and the future of democracy,” Sanjay Jha says.
“And I believe it is very likely that the DMK and Arvind Kejriwal will join, because this is the time to put aside any petty squabbles and think of the larger goal of the country,” he adds.But this may be easier said than done. The Congress and the AAP are the main rivals in Punjab, where assembly elections are due early next year. The two parties are already engaged in a bitter war of words in Punjab, where AAP is defending its only government and the Congress is going all out to defeat Kejriwal’s party and reclaim its lost glory and government in the state.So, let’s see if this political compulsion decides the future course of ties between the two parties or the “larger goal of the country”?

Moldova ready to take in more Ukrainian refugees come winter, Sandu says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
15:25:11 UTC
00:25:11 KST

Moldova is ready to take in more Ukrainian refugees this winter if Russia inflicts another humanitarian crisis upon the country through its targeted mass attacks, President Maia Sandu said on Oct. 8.
"Since 2022, more than one million Ukrainians fleeing the war have arrived in Moldova, and around 100,000 have found a home here. If this winter in Ukraine is as difficult as the whole world expects, we are ready to receive as many people as need safety," Sandu said at the Moldova Security Forum in Chisinau, as reported by Moldovan media outlet Newsmaker.
Russia's targeting of Ukraine's energy infrastructure last winter led to prolonged blackouts and heating outages across the country during sub-zero temperatures.
Speaking about preparations for the coming winter, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said Ukraine is better prepared than last year, but warned that Russia has strengthened its own capabilities by stockpiling jet-powered drones and missiles.
At the Moldova Security Forum, former Moldovan Prime Minister and current Presidential Special Envoy Dorin Recean also said that Moldova is preparing for the coming winter logistics-wise, as Ukraine and Moldova's energy grids are interconnected.
Moldova has dealt with repeated violations of its airspace during Russia's attacks against Ukraine.
After five Russian Banderol missiles and drones, exploded on the country's territory during the overnight attack against Ukraine on Oct. 3, Sandu warned that "(Russia's) war is dangerously reaching Moldova."
In response to the growing threat, Moldova announced on Oct. 7 that it plans to build protective shelters at border crossings with Ukraine where border guards and people in nearby areas can take cover during drone incursions.
