The government lifted its full-year growth projection to 1.3%, up from its April forecast of just 0.5%, as the German economy proved more resilient than expected.
Foreign trade is expected to boost Europe's biggest economy this year.
Stronger exports helped prompt the German government to more than double its growth forecast for this year on Thursday, as it said the economy had withstood the energy shock caused by the Iran war and was benefiting from the global AI boom.
The improved outlook could take some pressure off Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who is facing criticism that he has not done enough to kickstart the long-stagnant economy.
"The German economy proved more robust than projected in the spring," Economy Minister Katherina Reiche said as she announced the new forecasts.
"Despite geopolitical uncertainties, despite a global energy price shock, despite the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and despite tariffs, the economy was able to embark on a path of recovery," she told a press conference.
Germany's economy has faced years of stagnation amid weak export demand, high energy costs, US tariffs and Chinese competition, though recent indicators suggest it is starting to recover.
Reiche said foreign importers had rushed to stockpile German-made goods such as steel, fertiliser and aluminium in the months following the outbreak of the Iran war, supporting growth.
The government expects exports to grow by 3.7% this year, reversing a 0.9% decline in 2025.
German suppliers were also benefiting from the "global trend of investment in artificial intelligence", she said.
The boom in data centre construction has led to a surge in orders for German-made equipment such as lasers, semiconductor machinery and cooling systems, she said.
The economy ministry also raised its forecast for 2027 to 1.1%, from 0.9% previously, and said increased public spending on defence and infrastructure would support the economy in the coming years. Growth is expected to slow to 0.6% in 2028.
But it warned that household consumption would remain subdued as higher energy costs push up consumer prices. German inflation hit 3.3% in September, the highest level in nearly three years.
The ministry expects inflation to average 2.7% this year and rise to 3.0% in 2027, while household spending is forecast to grow by just 0.3% and 0.5%, respectively, after adjusting for inflation.
As in other countries, Germany has seen fuel costs surge amid the Iran war, prompting the government last week to announce a temporary fuel tax cut to provide some relief for drivers.
The official growth forecast for 2026 is in line with recent estimates by Germany's leading economic research institutes.

South Korea Investigates Fuel Shipments to Russia as Sanctioned Tankers Face Legal Scrutiny

- Category

South Korea Investigates Fuel Shipments to Russia as Sanctioned Tankers Face Legal Scrutiny
South Korea announced on October 8 that it could take legal action if an investigation finds that fuel shipments from its ports to Russia violated domestic law.
The Guardian reported the development after previously identifying more than 176,000 tonnes of fuel loaded at South Korean ports onto tankers that subsequently traveled to Russia.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
In a joint statement, South Korea’s foreign and trade ministries and customs service stated they were “checking additional information concerning the loading cases reported by the Guardian.” The agencies added that if violations are confirmed, the government "plans to act in accordance with the law."
The Guardian’s analysis of port records and ship-tracking data found that the fuel, mostly diesel, was loaded during July and August. Seven tankers made 14 voyages to Russia’s Far East, including three vessels under UK and EU sanctions.
South Korean authorities emphasized that loading refined petroleum products at domestic ports does not, by itself, violate the country’s export controls on Russia. Seoul also stated that it had not confirmed whether the cargo was South Korean-origin fuel and reported no customs-cleared exports of diesel, aviation fuel, or motor gasoline to Russia.
The investigation will examine the tankers’ actual routes, discrepancies with their declared destinations, and the reasons for those changes. Three sanctioned tankers reportedly declared Japan or Singapore as their destinations before traveling to Vladivostok.
The Russian-flagged Aram Khachaturian, which is not under Western sanctions, loaded cargo in Ulsan three times in July and August. On each voyage, the tanker declared a destination outside Russia before later sailing there.
The dispute has also intensified tensions between Kyiv and Seoul. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry confirmed this week that it had raised the shipments through closed diplomatic channels and requested an explanation, while South Korea announced on October 8 that it would recall its ambassador to Ukraine.
The fuel shipments come as Ukrainian strikes continue to pressure Russia’s domestic refining sector. The Guardian reported that Russian refinery throughput fell in June to its lowest level in more than 20 years, while diesel output was nearly 30% lower year over year, according to the International Energy Agency.
South Korean fuel had already surfaced in Russia's supply chain weeks earlier, after retaliatory Ukrainian strikes on refineries cut aviation fuel output and pushed Moscow to temporarily ban its own jet fuel exports.
By late August, three shadow-fleet tankers had delivered about 70,000 metric tons of Jet A-1 from South Korea and Egypt to ports in St. Petersburg and Vladivostok. The South Korean supply chain ran through UAE-based Caliph Energy Trading FZE. The fuel is suitable for Su-34, Su-35S, and Su-57 aircraft, as well as Tu-95MS strategic bombers.

Arsenal talent Max Dowman received three honors at once from Guinness World Records
Kyiv • UNN
Arsenal midfielder Max Dowman became the youngest player to make a Champions League debut and the youngest goalscorer in the Premier League. He is also the youngest English champion.
English midfielder of London’s "Arsenal" Max Dowman received three Guinness World Records distinctions at once. The young "Gunners" talent became the youngest debutant in the Champions League, as well as the youngest goalscorer in the Premier League. The Guinness World Records reports this, UNN reports.
Details
According to Guinness World Records, judge Caitlin Hiyem visited "Arsenal’s" training ground to present Max Dowman with three certificates for a record-breaking season.
Dowman received his first certificate as the youngest player in Champions League history. At the age of 15 years and 308 days, the Englishman made his debut for "Arsenal" in a Champions League group-stage match against Prague’s "Slavia," which ended 3–0.
The Englishman received his second certificate as the youngest goalscorer in the Premier League. In a match against England’s "Everton," for whom Vitaliy Mykolenko plays, Dowman broke forward on a counterattack in stoppage time, carried the ball 60 metres from his own half, and then rolled it into an empty net, sealing a 2–0 victory.
The "Gunners" not only secured another valuable three points, but Max also broke the record for the youngest goalscorer in the English Premier League at the age of 16 years and 73 days.
Also last season, "Arsenal" won the Premier League for the first time in 22 years. Max received his winner’s medal at the age of 16 years and 144 days, becoming the youngest footballer to win the Premier League. He surpassed the previous record held by Phil Foden of "Manchester City" by more than a year.
In addition, Dowman was included in the "Class of 2027" list—a selection of 30 "brightest young talents in men’s and women’s football," prepared for the release of the Guinness World Records Football Edition 2027.
Alongside Dowman, the "Class of 2027" list also includes "Barcelona" winger Lamine Yamal, "Manchester City" midfielder Ayoub Bouaddi, and "Chelsea" goalkeeper Hannah Hampton.

Russia’s main tank manufacturer—and the country’s only plant producing new T-90M tanks—is increasingly being used to rebuild heavily damaged vehicles recovered from the war in Ukraine, potentially diverting factory capacity from new production and complicating estimates of how many fresh tanks Moscow is actually building, according to Defence Blog on October 8.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Uralvagonzavod, or UVZ, in Nizhny Tagil is receiving battlefield-damaged T-90Ms for major overhauls, according to Defence Blog. Recent photographs showed a train carrying several badly damaged tanks toward the factory, with some vehicles displaying extensive structural damage.
Repairs may be competing with new tank production
Such work was traditionally handled by Russia’s network of military armored repair plants, known as BTRZ facilities, rather than by the country’s primary tank manufacturer.
Armor analyst Andrei Tarasenko, known as btbv.info, argues that the repair system has deteriorated to the point that UVZ is now taking on jobs outside its main production role.
“Damaged T-90Ms on the way to UVZ. Having ruined the BTRZ system, the monopoly corporation is also engaged in capital repairs that are completely outside its core business, since under factory conditions (not at a BTRZ) a repair costs as much as a new tank,” Tarasenko wrote.
Defence Blog noted that the development matters because UVZ is simultaneously responsible for manufacturing new T-90Ms and modernizing older Russian tanks.
Sending heavily damaged vehicles through the same industrial system can consume labor, workshop capacity, components, and time that could otherwise be devoted to new production.
How many “new” T-90Ms are actually rebuilt tanks?
Defence Blog noted that Oryx lead analyst Jakub Janovsky raised another issue: tanks extensively rebuilt at UVZ could make Russian production statistics harder to interpret, particularly if refurbished vehicles receive upgrades during the process.
“On the other hand, some organizations might end up counting factory repairs (and/or any additional upgrades) of these tanks as ‘new production,’” Janovsky wrote.
That distinction matters as analysts try to determine whether Russia’s defense industry is genuinely replacing battlefield losses with newly manufactured tanks or increasingly relying on restored and modernized vehicles from existing stocks.
Janovsky noted that whether a damaged tank can be recovered at all depends heavily on where it is disabled. Tanks knocked out in the contested gray zone are often struck repeatedly before Russian recovery crews can reach them, while vehicles damaged farther behind the front can be evacuated and returned to repair facilities much more easily.
Russia still shipping T-90Ms—but the production picture gets murkier
The growing repair burden comes as Russia’s armored industry continues to face pressure from Western sanctions, shortages of skilled labor, and the depletion of Soviet-era equipment reserves.
Some T-90Ms leaving UVZ have already been identified as using refurbished hulls from older T-90A tanks rather than entirely new hulls, further blurring the line between new construction, modernization, and reconstruction.
Uralvagonzavod has also publicly promoted its ability to restore heavily damaged tanks. In 2024, the company said it returned one T-90M to service in just four weeks after the vehicle had reportedly been hit by 26 drones.
The factory continues to deliver T-90Ms and upgraded T-72B3Ms to the Russian military. According to Defence Blog, earlier this week, UVZ announced another shipment of both types fitted with additional protection against drone strikes, although it did not disclose the number of tanks delivered.
Some newer T-90Ms have also appeared with the Arena-M active protection system, which Russian forces demonstrated intercepting attacking drones during the Tsentr-2026 exercise.
Earlier, Ukraine’s 423rd Separate Unmanned Systems Regiment knocked out a Russian T-54 tank, which traces its origins to the immediate post-World War II period and carries a 100mm main gun, making it one of the oldest mass-produced tank designs Russia has pulled from long-term storage and returned to wartime use.

EU to launch training and support mission for Lebanese army: foreign policy chief
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
13:23:10 UTC
22:23:10 KST

Melike Pala
08 October 2026•Update: 08 October 2026
The European Union is set to establish a new mission to train and advise the Lebanese armed forces, the bloc's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Thursday, stressing that the mission will not replace the UN peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon.
Speaking at a press conference with Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Rajji in Beirut, Kallas said planning for the EU's new support mission had been completed and that the bloc had received a formal invitation from Lebanese authorities.
She said she expected EU foreign ministers to formally establish the mission on Oct. 12.
"It will advise and assist the Lebanese armed forces and internal security forces to strengthen territorial control, border security, and also internal security," she said, stressing that the mission would operate in line with UN Security Council Resolution 1701 and would not serve as a replacement for the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL).
Kallas said UNIFIL had played an important role in Lebanon for almost five decades, adding that discussions were underway about the future of the UN presence in southern Lebanon.
"There cannot be a security vacuum when UNIFIL leaves Lebanon," she warned.
She said European countries currently contributing troops to UNIFIL could potentially contribute to a future international force, but stressed that such a force would require a UN mandate.
Kallas also linked Lebanon's stability to developments in neighboring Syria, welcoming stronger cooperation between Beirut and Damascus.

Germany news: UK's Burnham visits Berlin for talks with Merz

IN DEPTH: New naval port aims to enhance Germany's defense capabilities
Citing the escalating security threat, Germany's Navy has decided to establish a second port on the North Sea coast.
After months of evaluating locations, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said the Bundeswehr's new naval port would be built in Emden.
"Emden offers ideal conditions, such as quick access to the Atlantic Ocean and the far north," Pistorius said.
Read all about why Pistorius said Germany needs another port for its navy and why Emden should host it: A new naval port in Emden aims to enhance Germany's defense capabilities
Steinmeier reassures France over Germany's EU commitment
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier has pledged that Germany will remain firmly committed to Europe, seeking to reassure France following recent gains by the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in state elections.
Speaking during a state visit to Paris on Thursday, Steinmeier said Germany could succeed only as a European country firmly embedded in the European Union.
"Germans will remain good Europeans," Steinmeier said at the Elysee Palace, alongside French President Emmanuel Macron.
After bilateral talks, Steinmeier emphasized that Germany "can only be successful as a European Germany, that is, tightly embedded in the European Union.
"That is true, and it will remain so for us," the German president said in Paris.
His remarks followed recent electoral successes by the euroskeptic AfD, including in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt, which have prompted concern in France.
Steinmeier described the current period as "damn difficult," pointing to the war in Ukraine, geopolitical challenges and domestic political tensions in both countries.
"We are experiencing a polarization of society, with the strengthening of the radical fringes," he said.
He warned that this was making it increasingly difficult to form governments and govern effectively, particularly as political debate shifted toward social media.
Macron also spoke of a “time of upheaval."
"We are witnessing how social media is accelerating societal changes and fueling doubts over democracy," he said. "If Germany and France do not move forward together, Europe will not make any progress at all."
Steinmeier was welcomed with military honors by Macron at the Arc de Triomphe, where he laid flowers at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier and rekindled its memorial flame.
At the Elysee Palace, the two presidents attended the signing of an agreement to bring the Franco-German Citizens' Fund under the umbrella of the Franco-German Youth Office. The fund supports cross-border civil society projects and has an annual budget of €5 million ($5.8 million).
On Friday, both presidents will travel to Bordeaux. There, the focus will be on defense and military cooperation.
German spy agency BND approved suspect's side job
Germany's foreign intelligence agency reportedly approved outside work by an employee for a former spy chief who is now suspected of illegally obtaining classified information.
According to German news magazine Der Spiegel, the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) officially authorized Manfred D. to work for former BND head August Hanning, who became a private-sector consultant after leaving government service in 2009.
Prosecutors allege that Manfred D. supplied Hanning with nearly 2,000 internal BND documents, many of them classified, which the former intelligence chief allegedly used for commercial gain.
Investigators believe the arrangement began around 2010, when Hanning and his former chief of staff allegedly agreed that intelligence would be supplied in return for payment.
Manfred D. allegedly passed the documents to Hanning between 2010 and 2022.
Hanning, 80, headed the BND from 1998 to 2005. He is suspected of offenses including intelligence-agent activity, espionage involving state secrets and attempted treason.
Manfred D., 64, served as chief of staff to several BND presidents from March 2012 until March 2026, a position that gave him access to sensitive intelligence.
He is accused of aiding attempted treason and espionage involving state secrets.
Both men have been held in pretrial detention since this week.
According to Der Spiegel, the BND had known about Manfred D.'s work for Hanning for some time and had issued an official authorization for the secondary employment.
The agency declined to answer questions about when the authorization was granted or what activities it covered, the magazine said.
Hanning's lawyer has denied wrongdoing, saying his client was being prosecuted unjustly.
He acknowledged that Hanning had possessed confidential documents but denied he had passed on information detrimental to Germany or had done so for payment.
Merz, Burnham inaugurate new German-British friendship treaty
Chancellor Friedrich Merz received relatively new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham with military honors in Berlin.
During Burnham's visit, the new Treaty on Friendship and Bilateral Cooperation between the UK and Germany — signed last year by previous Prime Minister Keir Starmer — officially comes into force.
Aslo known as the Kensington Treaty, the 27-page document lays out a 17-point action plan for closer cooperation in the post-Brexit era, with the UK no longer a part of the EU.
Merz called it a historic day and said the deal opened up new opportunities for bilateral cooperation, particularly for students and young people.
"That's what we're doing this for," Merz said. "So that the young generation also notices when it comes to bilateral relations between Germany as part of the EU and the UK, how well we Europeans work together and how much we belong together, too."
Burnham said that the Kensington Treaty would improve security in Europe, help both economies grow and improve people's living standards.
"In challenging times, and these are challenging times, we need the strongest possible cooperation with our closest partners and Germany really is one of our closest partners," the former mayor of Manchester said.
Burnham also said that he was open to Germany joining the GCAP program, a partnership between Britain, Italy and Japan to build a next-generation multirole combat aircraft.
"I've indicated to the chancellor ... our openness to Germany joining GCAP," he said at a press conference. "That is something that we seek to progress in the coming period, working with our other partners, Italy and Japan."
A rival Franco-German plan to build a next-generation military jet, FCAS, collapsed in June.
The GCAP project has been set up to allow for different levels of involvement. It expanded in July when Canada signed up as an observer, and Saudi Arabia had also been touted as a potential interested party.
Germany already works with the UK and Italy on the joint Eurofighter Typhoon project.
Italy and Japan would need to join Burnham in indicating a willingness for Germany participating in this project.
Left-leaning parties in Berlin to begin talks on forming new government
Germany's Left Party, Greens and Social Democrats (SPD) have agreed to begin exploratory talks on forming a coalition government in Berlin, two and a half weeks after the city's state election.
The breakthrough follows an agreement on combating antisemitism and organized crime, issues that had threatened to derail negotiations before they began.
The parties said they would protect Jewish life in Berlin and reaffirmed that Israel's right to exist was "non-negotiable."
They also agreed to strengthen the police and domestic intelligence services in their efforts to protect Jewish communities.
Party and parliamentary group members who violate the agreed principles could face expulsion, with the relevant parliamentary group responsible for deciding and publicly explaining any disciplinary measures.
The three parties also pledged to maintain a clear distance from individuals and groups associated with organized crime.
The Greens and SPD had made agreements on antisemitism, racism and organized crime conditions to open talks with the Left Party.
Those demands followed controversy over positions on Israel and the Palestinians held by some members of Berlin's Left Party.
Concerns intensified after an election-night gathering organized by the Left's Neukölln branch was attended by a figure associated with a partly criminal clan and a controversial pro-Palestinian activist.
The activist is alleged to have links to the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine, which the European Union designates as a terrorist organization.
The Left Party emerged as the strongest party in Berlin's September 20 election, winning 25.7% of the vote.
It hopes to form a coalition with the Greens and SPD, potentially making its parliamentary co-leader Elif Eralp Berlin's first mayor from the Left Party.

The latest exhibit at Madame Tussauds in Berlin would surely taste just as dire as all the others, but the wax replica of a döner kebab is at least supposed to look appetizing.
The kebab — obviously stuffed "with everything" or "mit alles/mit allem," depending on your level of German grammatical exactitude — is complemented by a recreation of the popular snack stop Mustafa's Gemüse Kebap in Berlin's Kreuzberg district.
Tarik Kara, who owns the restaurant, was present in the flesh for Thursday's unveiling.

Low-cost carrier Ryanair cuts flights in Germany, with Berlin hardest-hit
Irish airline Ryanair says it will be offering 700,000 fewer seats on flights in Germany this winter season, citing the "astronomical" cost of various charges, including for air traffic control and security.
This represents a reduction of 10%.
Ryanair said Berlin Brandenburg Airport, which it has dubbed "Europe's least successful airport," would be affected the most, losing around half of its current services from the airline.
Among the 12 routes to be axed in Berlin are those to Gran Canaria, Palermo, Marseille and Thessaloniki.
The Ryanair base at the airport is set to close on October 24. Seven aircraft and their crews are to be relocated to more competitive airports in other European countries, the company said.
Passengers in the German capital will now have much less choice and considerably higher fares, according to the airline's chief executive Eddie Wilson.
Hamburg will see a cut of 5%, but Memmingen and Cologne will have their capacity expanded.
Ryanair's winter schedule also adds regional airports in Saarbrücken and Friedrichshafen.
Sick leave for mental illnesses on the rise — health insurer
The number of days of sick leave in Germany on grounds of psychological problems has risen some 42% in the last 10 years, the AOK health insurance company says.
According to AOK, there were 284 days of sick leave per 100 members in 2015, compared with 403 per 100 members in 2025.
Although absences from work are much more frequently due to respiratory illnesses, those prompted by mental illness tend to be much longer, AOK said.
It said that on average, employees took 28.5 days off on grounds of psychological problems last year compared with 5.7 days because of respiratory illnesses.
However, the AOK said there had been a slight reduction in the average number of days of sick leave taken by employees, from 23.9 in 2023 and 2024 to 23.3 in 2025.
The highest level, 24.5 days, was reached in 2022 during the coronavirus pandemic.

The Qilin group, one of the most "aggressive" cybercrime organizations according to auhtories, has extorted about $2.9 billion from some 4,000 companies and institutions worldwide since 2024. At least 30 companies in the German state of NRW have been affected.
Hacking the hackers
German police infiltrated the Qilin group and monitored its members for several months. NRW Justice Minister Benjamin Limbach said that payments and cryptocurrency transactions were traced to individuals linked to the organization.
The Russian group is also blamed for an attack on Britain's National Health Service (NHS) that disrupted more than 10,000 medical appointments. Last year, shares of Japanese brewer Asahi fell after Qilin carried out a cyberattack that disrupted the company's ordering and delivery systems.
According to authorities, Russian cyberattacks against Germany have increased since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
My lifelong Pokemon collection is worth around €400,000, Christoph Kramer estimates
Retired midfielder and 2014 World Cup winner Christoph Kramer — now a TV presenter, podcaster and novelist — discusses another of his longstanding passions in an interview with the dpa news agency published on Thursday.
He may not have caught them all in more than a quarter of a century hunting Pokemon cards, but he's corralled a collection of creatures capable of dropping the jaw of a typical 10-year-old.
"I've been collecting pokemon cards since 1999, I have the complete first edition in English and would not give up my collection for any price," the 36-year-old said. "I'm wholly convinced that our generation won't be hanging classical paintings on the walls aged 50 or 60 any more, but instead will prefer to frame their Pokemon cards behind glass," he said.
Kramer, who might be best known as the World Cup winner with no memory of his finest hour on the pitch because of a concussion sustained during the 2014 final against Argentina, has quickly graduated to a senior broadcasting and punditry role since quitting football.
He's currently promoting his second novel, called "Wolkenberührpunkt," which one could perhaps translate as "the point touching the clouds." As he told dpa, he's always had a passion for collecting more generally.
"I got myself an original iPhone in its original packaging and laminated. Objects like collectors' cards, rare vintage gear or retro jerseys are, for me, the real art of our era," Kramer said. "Of course it has a lot to do with nostalgia, because these are things from my childhood I simply love."
Spanish and Turkish make gains among school language learners
Although English remains by far the most-learned foreign language at German schools, Spanish and Turkish are becoming ever more popular, while French, Latin and Russian are losing ground, new figures show.
Turkish is being learned by almost three times as many pupils as 20 years ago, with 29,230 of altogether 8.9 million school students taking the language in 2025/2026 (0.31%).
That compares with some 13,000 pupils out of 9.5 million in 2005/2006 (0.13%), according to the Federal Statistical Office (Destatis).
There are also twice as many Spanish learners at German schools compared with two decades ago.
Some 549,000 of the current 8.9 million pupils took the language as a subject in 2025/2026 (6.1%), compared with 243,400 of the 9.5 million pupils back in 2005/2006 (2.56%), Destatis said.
Fewer pupils are learning French than 20 years ago, even if the language is second only to English in the statistics.
Some 14% of pupils learned French in the 2025/2026 school year, compared with 17% in 2005/2006.
Latin and Russian are also being learned by ever fewer pupils, with the former falling from 8.1% of schoolchildren to some 6% over the 20-year period, and the latter now learned by 0.746% compared with 1.25% in 2005/2006.
English remains far ahead at the top of the language-learning table, despite a small decline over the past two decades.
It was learned by 81% of pupils back in 2005/2006 compared with 78% in 2025/2026.
Suspected puma on the loose eludes searchers
Police have so far been unsuccessful in their search for a suspicious animal sighted near Munich airport on Tuesday that is thought to possibly be a puma.
Thermal imaging cameras employed in an overnight aerial search failed to detect any sign of the animal in the Notzingermoos nature reserve in the district of Erding, a police spokeswoman said.
During the light hours of Wednesday, police also scoured the area with the help of a helicopter and drones in addition to officers on the ground but in vain.
There was one false alarm after a security guard spotted a suspicious animal on surveillance footage, with a helicopter sent to investigate.
That animal is believed to have been a domestic cat, police said.
The searches began after a hunter spotted and filmed a suspicious animal using a night-vision device late on Tuesday evening, with an expert who viewed the footage later saying it was possibly a puma.
However, local authorities have noted that there has so far been no definite identification of the animal.

Solar parks driving electricity price down but could result in higher transmission charges

Unknown Publisher

Solar parks driving electricity price down but could result in higher transmission charges
Sunny summers are bringing zero and negative prices to the electricity market with increasing frequency, raising questions for renewable energy developers about how they can recoup their investments.
Southern Estonia's largest solar park has begun operating at the former Raadi military airfield. With a capacity of 74 megawatts, the park could theoretically meet half the electricity needs of Tartu's households. However, summer sunshine and falling electricity prices pose a significant profitability risk for the producer.
"With projects like these, you certainly have to think very carefully about when to generate electricity, when to sell it and when to store it. There will certainly be quite a few instances when production has to be curtailed," said Kristo Seli, CEO of Estiko Group.
According to researchers, Estonia's electricity grid faces a paradox: While summer production drives down wholesale electricity prices, connecting additional power plants to the grid brings new costs for consumers.
"When we add power plants or solar parks and they generate more energy, that should bring electricity prices down. At the same time, additional equipment is being added to the grid, making it more complex, and that could lead to higher network fees," said Ivo Palu, a professor at Tallinn University of Technology's (TalTech) Department of Electrical Power Engineering and Mechatronics.
The main problem is the mismatch between when electricity is generated and when it is consumed.
"We can't take the sunshine from Midsummer Day and bring it with us to Christmas. That would require different kinds of solutions," said Toomas Plank, director of the University of Tartu's Institute of Physics.
Although energy storage is increasingly needed to balance the grid, the government does not plan to impose mandatory requirements on developers, instead leaving it to market prices to drive investment.
"It also makes much more economic sense to build hybrid parks. When the sun is shining, you can generate cheap electricity from solar panels, store it and then sell it on the market when prices peak. Both the developer and, in the long run, the consumer benefit, with consumers getting lower electricity prices," said Minister of Energy and the Environment Erkki Keldo.
Estiko plans to build a large-scale battery storage facility at Raadi by the middle of next summer. The Raadi project thus demonstrates that the future of solar energy lies in hybrid solutions that help keep electricity prices reasonable even when the sun is not shining.
--

EU expects enlargement “Super Tuesday”: reminded of importance for Hungary of Ukraine’s law on national minorities
Kyiv • UNN
The EU is preparing intergovernmental conferences on the accession of Ukraine and other countries and seeks to open the internal market and competitiveness clusters for it. The decision depends on the law on national minorities.
Another "Super Tuesday" on EU enlargement is scheduled for October 13 following the meeting of the EU General Affairs Council. The European Union plans to hold a series of intergovernmental conferences to advance accession negotiations, including with Ukraine, and approval of two clusters is expected after a vote in the Verkhovna Rada on national minorities. ANSA reports this, citing sources, UNN writes.
Details
Ukraine’s goal, as stated, is to open clusters 2 ("Internal Market") and 3 ("Competitiveness and Inclusive Growth").
An EU diplomatic source notes that although the aim is to open these two clusters, "the situation is still evolving." The issue of national minorities is particularly sensitive in Hungary. The Council is currently considering legislation implementing the agreement reached between Budapest and Kyiv, and this is "an important step regarding Hungary’s position on opening the clusters," according to the source.
"We understand that the Council will consider this legislation by next Monday," officials said at the EU General Affairs Council ahead of its meeting.
Accession negotiations with Albania, Montenegro, and Moldova are also expected to advance. Montenegro, the candidate that has progressed furthest in the accession process, hopes to close several chapters.
However, it is currently reported that there is "full green light for two chapters, while work on several others is still ongoing."

France Develops IRIFI Strike Drone With Range Of 2,000 km — Morocco to Be First Customer
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
13:20:05 UTC
22:20:05 KST

French defense company Harmattan AI has unveiled the new long-range IRIFI strike drone, with Morocco set to be its first customer.
Harmattan AI has provided details on the new drone’s specifications.
The IRIFI UAV is designed to deliver high-precision strikes at ranges of up to 2,000 kilometers. The drones will be launched from mobile container-based launchers, allowing for rapid deployment and use in large numbers.
The drone is equipped with an autonomous navigation system that does not rely on GNSS satellite signals, as well as an optical guidance system for the final phase of flight. According to the developer, this ensures resistance to electronic warfare and strike accuracy down to one meter.
Before launch, the operator identifies the target and route, after which the drone autonomously carries out the mission without constant communication with the ground control station.
Harmattan AI positions the IRIFI as a relatively inexpensive means of delivering massive, high-precision strikes. The company has not yet disclosed the warhead’s weight, the drone’s speed, dimensions, or cost.
According to the developers’ plan, a single operator will be able to manage the deployment of dozens of such drones. Artificial intelligence will be used to plan strikes by analyzing satellite imagery. However, the decision to engage targets will remain with a human operator.
The French publication Le Desk reports that on October 7, during the Marrakech Air Show, representatives of the Moroccan Defense Ministry and Harmattan AI signed a letter of intent regarding the procurement, joint development, and production of the IRIFI within the kingdom.
As part of the collaboration, production facilities for the new UAVs are to be established in Morocco. In particular, critical technological components are planned to be developed and manufactured directly in the country with the involvement of local specialists.
At the same time, the signed document is currently a letter of intent, not a final supply contract. The number of drones planned for procurement, the cost of the program, and the timeline for the start of serial production have not been disclosed.
The new program builds on the strategic partnership established in June 2026 between Harmattan AI and the Royal Moroccan Armed Forces. The initial agreements called for the establishment of local production of autonomous defense systems, a research and development center for artificial intelligence, and collaboration with educational institutions.
Earlier, Militarnyi reported that in October 2025, Ukraine’s Skyeton and France’s Harmattan AI announced a partnership to integrate artificial intelligence technologies into Raybird drones.
In February 2026, it was also reported that Harmattan AI planned to integrate its compact Sahara synthetic aperture radars into Ukrainian drones. These radars enable reconnaissance even in cloudy and foggy conditions.

Attack risks rise for tankers as Iran vows to block more Hormuz routes

Attack risks rise for tankers as Iran vows to block more Hormuz routes
- Iran has warned it may block unauthorised Hormuz routes, raising attack risks for tankers and threatening oil exports from regional rivals.
- A tanker, the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged Acers, was hit near Qatar, with minor crew injuries and fears of a wider combat zone.
- Shipping and oil markets are under growing strain, with lower vessel traffic, tighter oil stocks, and higher costs as the conflict spreads.
AI generated
LONDON – Tankers are facing a higher risk of attacks and intimidation as they try to get critical shipments through the Strait of Hormuz after Iran issued new warnings it would block routes that it has not authorised, sources said.
Last week already saw the biggest number of attacks on tankers in the key waterway since the Iran war began – cutting the number of vessels trying to get through to the lowest in more than two months.
Iran has now warned regional countries that any attempt to open new routes for oil exports would be considered hostile, a senior regional official close to Tehran told Reuters.
It was part of a plan agreed by both Iran’s political leaders and its Revolutionary Guards, the official added.
‘Policy of fear and threats’
“Iran has absolutely no intention of allowing control of the Strait of Hormuz to slip from its hands and has plans ready to block routes that some regional countries have for exporting oil,” a senior diplomat in the region briefed by Tehran told Reuters separately.
“This could involve missile and drone attacks on ships, or sending boats to scare ships away,” the diplomat added. “It plans to continue this policy of fear and threats,” he said.
In recent months, Gulf oil producers have rushed shipments of oil through channels that hug the Omani side of the strait before transferring the oil in open waters in the Gulf of Oman with aerial support from the US, sources said.
In the latest incident in the past 24 hours, projectiles struck a tanker some 51 nautical miles off the coast of Qatar inside the Gulf, British navy agency UKMTO reported.
Maritime security sources said the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged chemical tanker Acers had been hit by multiple projectiles north of Qatar’s Madinat ash Shamal, with minor injuries sustained by its crew.
“The Acers strike raises the prospect of a wider combat area affecting approaches to Qatar, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq,” maritime risk intelligence group Pole Star Global’s subsidiary Clearwater Dynamics said in a report on Oct 8.
The vessel’s operator, listed in shipping databases as Antigua and Barbuda-based Valvoria Shipping, could not be reached for comment.
“The recent spate of Iranian attacks seems to have dampened the appetite of shipowners to sail through the Strait,” said Jakob Larsen, chief safety & security officer at shipping association BIMCO.
“The Iranian threat appears to have increased.”
‘War at sea does not remain at sea’
US President Donald Trump is weighing next steps against Iran, including whether to escalate strikes before or after the November midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress, as he presses a naval blockade meant to pile economic pressure on Tehran to reach a deal to end the conflict.
The war – and its US$3 billion (S$3.85 billion) monthly price tag – has become a key issue on the campaign trail.
Governments and energy companies have drawn oil from stockpiles to alleviate pressure in a global oil market facing unprecedented supply disruptions in 2026, also caused by the war in Ukraine.
The amount of oil in storage that is accessible to the global market is running low, industry executives said at a forum in London this week, making the market more fragile and putting upward pressure on prices.
The impact of the crisis was increasingly rippling across the global economy. Danish shipping group Maersk said on Oct 8 it was increasing its emergency fuel surcharge on inland transportation in the UK and Ireland due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
“There is no going back to the old world, no harbouring back to the stability and the prosperity of the last several decades,” Major-General Paul Maynard, assistant chief of the naval staff with Britain’s Royal Navy, told a UK Chamber of Shipping Riviera conference in London this week.
“A war at sea does not remain at sea.” REUTERS

Full UAH 20 mln bail paid for Mudra – HACC
Ukraine

2026-10-08
16:19:20 EEST
22:19:20 KST

Bail of UAH 20 million set by the court as an alternative to detention has been paid in full for former deputy head of the Office of the President Iryna Mudra, who is suspected in cases involving money laundering and raiding, the High Anti-Corruption Court (HACC) told Interfax-Ukraine.
"The bail has been paid in full," the court said on Thursday.
On August 25, the HACC ordered Mudra's detention with an alternative of UAH 20 million bail. Mudra said she would try to raise the amount. The HACC Appeals Chamber subsequently upheld the decision. The bail had not been paid into the HACC account since then, and Mudra remained in pretrial detention.
On September 24, the HACC found that Mudra's rights had been violated and ordered the National Bank of Ukraine to determine why banks were refusing to accept the bail payment.
Earlier that day, the NBU said bank representatives had cited among the reasons for refusing such transactions the lack of documentary proof of the source of funds, including cash, splitting bail payments into multiple transactions and the use of shell companies to make payments.
The following day, the NBU said it had taken note of the HACC ruling concerning bail payments and would respond within its powers after receiving the official document.
On September 28, lawyers from Miller law firm, which represents Mudra, said the NBU had failed to comply with the September 24 HACC ruling ordering it to determine why banks were refusing to accept the bail.
On September 28, the HACC upheld Mudra's pretrial measure of detention with an alternative of UAH 20 million bail. Her defense had asked for the bail to be reduced to UAH 13 million, which had already been transferred to the court's account by that time.
On August 19, the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU) and Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAPO) released a video about an operation codenamed Forest Gump, saying they had exposed and notified suspects of the laundering of UAH 150 million to pay bail for a suspect in the Midas case. The group included, among others, a deputy head of the Office of the President and a former member of parliament. Later that day, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed a decree dismissing Mudra as deputy head of the Office of the President.
On August 20, NABU and SAPO released a second video concerning corruption involving the same senior officials, codenamed Femida, describing the exposure of alleged illegal acquisition of real estate and corporate assets through forged documents. Mudra, a former deputy head of the Office of the President, also features in this episode.
Later on August 20, NABU and SAPO commented on the videos released earlier under the names Forest Gump and Femida concerning alleged corruption schemes involving senior officials of the Office of the President, a former and a current member of parliament. "The activities of the criminal organization were aimed, among other things, at acquiring high-value real estate and other assets of legal entities through unauthorized interference in the operation of information (automated) networks of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine, forgery of court decisions and title documents," NABU said in a Telegram post.
NABU also said that in June 2026, certain members of the alleged criminal organization, acting in collusion with representatives and officials of a state-owned bank, had organized and facilitated the laundering of criminal proceeds.
"Based on the evidence obtained, NABU detectives and SAPO prosecutors notified members of the criminal organization and persons they had involved of suspicion under Articles 255, 191, 206-2, 209, 358 and 361 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine," SAPO said.

This “golden tree” coral was too strange for any known family
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
13:18:54 UTC
22:18:54 KST

This “golden tree” coral was too strange for any known family
- Date:
- October 8, 2026
- Source:
- Pensoft Publishers
- Summary:
- A brilliant yellow coral discovered off Costa Rica proved so unusual that scientists had to create an entirely new family to classify it. The meter-tall colonies rise from seafloors covered in brittle stars, inspiring the Tolkien-inspired name Laurinque elenya, or “golden tree of the stars.” Advanced genetic analysis revealed that the coral belongs to a previously unknown evolutionary lineage.
- Share:
Scientists surveying underwater mountains off Costa Rica have identified a remarkable new coral that is unlike any known coral family. Its genetic makeup and physical features were so distinctive that researchers created an entirely new family to classify it. The bright yellow coral, which has a branching, tree-like appearance, was discovered between 360 and 529 meters below the Pacific Ocean's surface. The findings are reported in the open-access journal ZooKeys.
Some colonies grow more than a meter tall. Researchers collected specimens using the remotely operated vehicle SuBastian during expeditions in 2019 and 2023 aboard the research vessels Falkor and Falkor (too), which are operated by the Schmidt Ocean Institute. The expeditions explored seamounts near Isla del Coco and along Costa Rica's Pacific margin.
A Golden Coral Among Fields of Stars
The coral was especially abundant on rocky outcrops where brittle stars covered nearly every available surface. Against this shimmering backdrop, the bright yellow branches appeared to rise from the seafloor like glowing trees surrounded by stars.
That unusual scene helped inspire the scientific name. The new genus, Laurinque, is derived from "Laurinquë," which means "golden tree" in Quenya, the Elvish language created by J.R.R. Tolkien for The Lord of the Rings and The Silmarillion. Researchers selected the name because of the coral's vivid yellow color and tree-like shape.
Its species name, elenya, means "stellar" or "of the stars" in Quenya. The name refers to the dense populations of brittle stars surrounding the coral colonies. Together, the genus and species names reflect what the researchers described as an almost mystical elvish landscape on the deep ocean floor.
DNA Reveals a New Coral Family
Determining where the coral fit on the evolutionary family tree proved far more complicated than expected. Scientists initially sequenced three genes commonly used to identify and classify corals. Instead of pointing toward the same group, each gene suggested a different and unrelated family.
Because those results were unusually inconsistent, the researchers used phylogenomics, a method that compares hundreds of genes at the same time. The broader genetic analysis finally clarified the coral's evolutionary position.
The results showed that the species does not belong to any previously recognized coral family. It represents a distinct evolutionary lineage that is most closely related to Eunicellidae, but its genetics and anatomy differ enough to justify the creation of a new family called Laurinqueidae. Researchers also established the new genus Laurinque specifically for the species.
Dr. Odalisca Breedy of the Universidad de Costa Rica (lead researcher on the study) said:
"I saw the octocoral garden for the first time in 2019 and I was impressed by the beauty of the landscape, which inspired, later the elvish name of the taxa. I thought the species could belong to a known family and genera, but after the preliminar morphological analysis I realised that it was something very different that I could not match with the known taxa.
"In 2023 we collected more samples and thanks to the exhaustive molecular analyses made by my colleagues, Cathy McFadden, Catalina Murillo and Andrea Quattrini, we were able to determine the taxonomic placement of the stunning species, in one of the most enigmatic sites."
Costa Rica's Deep Sea Still Holds Surprises
Dr. Breedy led the research with an international team of collaborators. The Schmidt Ocean Institute supported the expeditions, along with a National Geographic Society research grant.
The find joins a growing number of previously undocumented species discovered on Costa Rica's seamounts. It also highlights how much of the deep ocean remains poorly explored, even though it covers roughly two-thirds of Earth's surface.
Coral gardens like this one are considered vulnerable marine ecosystems. Their complex three-dimensional structures provide habitat for many other forms of deep-sea life, making them important centers of biodiversity in environments that scientists are only beginning to understand.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Pensoft Publishers. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Odalisca Breedy, Catherine S. McFadden, Catalina Murillo-Cruz, Ana-Belén Yánez-Suárez, Katleen Robert, Andrea M. Quattrini. A coral among stars: A new octocoral family (Anthozoa, Octocorallia, Malacalcyonacea) from seamounts in the tropical eastern Pacific. ZooKeys, 2026; 1283: 253 DOI: 10.3897/zookeys.1283.191899

State budget 2027 reaches parliament with backing guaranteed by Socialist Party
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
13:18:50 UTC
22:18:50 KST

The government on Thursday submitted to parliament the 2027 state budget, projecting 2% growth and a surplus of 0.1–0.2% of GDP. Approval is assured, as the PS will abstain in the key vote.
On Thursday afternoon the Government submitted to Parliament the draft State Budget law for 2027, two days before the deadline, after approving it this morning in the Council of Ministers.
The document was handed over by the Minister of Finance, Joaquim Miranda Sarmento, to the Speaker of the Assembly of the Republic, José Pedro Aguiar-Branco.
The third State Budget of Luís Montenegro's government has its passage once again guaranteed by the Socialist Party (PS).
The Socialist leader, José Luís Carneiro, announced last week the intention to abstain in the first overall vote, which takes place on 28 October, after the prime minister, Luís Montenegro, gave assurances on four conditions set by the Socialists: a constitutional review with PS and PSD playing a central role, protection of current and future pensions, funding for investments left unfinished after the RRP, and support for the recovery of municipalities and regions affected by storms.
The detailed debate and vote will run between 29 October and 24 November, with the final overall vote scheduled for 24 November.
The PCP and the Left Bloc have already announced that they will vote against the Government's proposal. Chega has also threatened to vote against (source in Portuguese)if the prime minister refuses to lower the retirement age, and has put forward an additional demand to cut VAT on fuels and apply zero VAT to a basic basket of essential foodstuffs. These are red lines the Government has already rejected.
The remaining parties have not yet announced how they will vote.
The President of the Republic, António José Seguro, said on Thursday that he hoped for a "fruitful debate" to improve people's lives "at a very difficult time".
Speaking to journalists in Parliament after meetings with the parties on the Budget proposal, the Minister of Finance, Joaquim Miranda Sarmento, declined to say how much room there was for negotiations.
The Government estimates that the economic measures already adopted, which will continue to affect the public finances in 2027, will have a impact of 4.8 billion euros next year, still without taking into account any new policies to be included in the next Budget.
As for the macroeconomic scenario for next year, the Government is forecasting economic growth of 2%, in line with the pace seen in recent years, but representing a slight slowdown compared with the 2.3% expected for this year.
The Government is projecting a budget surplus of 0.1% of gross domestic product (GDP) next year.
In the document, the Ministry of Finance raises its inflation forecast for this year to 2.9% and expects a slowdown to 2.3% in 2027.
The Government also projects that public debt will fall to 84.5% of GDP in 2027, three percentage points less than the 87.5% estimated for this year.
The cost of financing public debt will weigh more heavily on the state's accounts, with the bill for interest rising by 23.2% to 8,217 million euros. That is equivalent to 2.4% of GDP, compared with 2% in 2026 and 2025.
Pensions, public-sector wages and debt interest are among the main sources of pressure, alongside tax measures such as the updating of personal income tax brackets, the reduction of the corporate tax rate and housing measures.
Measures on personal, corporate and property taxes
The Minister of Finance said that the 2027 Budget provides for a further cut in personal income tax, through the updating of tax brackets, the specific deduction and the minimum subsistence threshold, mechanisms which by law have to be adjusted.
The PSD/CDS-PP government has decided to lower personal income tax rates in the first to sixth brackets by between 0.3 and 0.5 percentage points, a measure with an estimated impact of 400 million euros, which will already be reflected in withholding tax in 2026.
The reduction will be 0.3 percentage points in the first bracket, 0.5 percentage points from the second to the fifth brackets, and again 0.3 percentage points in the sixth bracket.
The rates remain the same as those presented in September 2026, with retroactive effect.
The proposal also confirms a 3.88% update of personal income tax brackets next year, below the 4.5% pay rise in the private sector set out in the social concertation agreement.
In practice this means there is a risk that the tax burden will increase for taxpayers whose pay rises exceed 3.88%. Anyone earning more may be pushed into a higher tax bracket, paying more tax and seeing all or part of their pay rise eroded.
The minimum income exempt from personal income tax in the 2027 State Budget will track the minimum wage. The annual reference value for the minimum subsistence income is 13,580 euros, which divided by 14 months corresponds to 970 euros, the planned minimum wage in 2027.
Productivity bonuses, performance bonuses, profit-sharing and year-end bonuses will also be exempt from personal income tax "up to a limit of 6% of the worker's annual basic pay", according to the 2027 State Budget proposal.
The Government estimates that corporate tax revenue will fall by 99 million euros in 2027 compared with the projected outturn for 2026, a drop of 1%.
"This trend reflects the 1 percentage point cut in the corporate tax rate, whose impact on revenue should be partially offset by the expected growth in economic activity," the document states.
The revenue impact of the one percentage point cut is 300 million euros.
Last year the general corporate tax rate fell from 20% to 19%, which is the rate applied to companies' 2026 profits.
In 2027 the general rate will be cut by another point, from 19% to 18%, but this rate will apply only to 2027 profits, with an impact on the public finances in 2028.
The Government's goal is to bring the corporate tax rate down to 17% by 2028, cutting it by one percentage point a year. The rate will be 15% on the first 50,000 euros of profit for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
The corporate tax break for companies that increase average wages by at least 4.5% will also remain in place next year.
The proposal includes a 2.3% increase in the brackets of municipal property transfer tax (IMT) on the purchase of an urban property or autonomous unit used exclusively for housing, whether or not it is a primary residence.
The purchase of property up to 108,792 euros in value for use as a primary residence will be exempt from IMT. This represents an increase of 2,446 euros compared with this year's threshold of 106,346 euros.
The Government also expects to raise an extra 300 million euros in taxes in 2027 from anti-fraud measures on fuel approved this year.
The State Budget proposal also envisages a 5.2% increase in receipts from the tax on petroleum products (ISP), reaching 3,796 million euros. The Government attributes this growth to private consumption. For 2026, ISP revenue is expected to be 3,610 million euros.
The Government is also forecasting for 2027 an increase of 139 million euros (8.1%) in revenue from tobacco tax, rising to 1,864 million euros.
Revenue from the tax on alcohol, alcoholic beverages and drinks with added sugar or other sweeteners (IABA) is expected to grow by 27 million euros (7.5%), to 392 million euros.
Minimum income, minimum wage and civil service
The document also confirms a 50-euro increase in the solidarity supplement for the elderly (CSI) in 2027, with the reference amount rising to 720 euros.
The Government's programme envisages this reaching 870 euros in 2029, up from the current 670 euros.
This strengthening of the CSI will have an impact of 100 million euros entered in next year's Budget.
Total social security spending on support for the most vulnerable older people is budgeted at 709 million euros in 2027, 38 million more than the amount budgeted last year.
A rise in the minimum wage from 920 to 970 euros is also planned. The tripartite agreement on pay and economic growth for 2025-2028, signed in October 2024 between the Government, the four employers' confederations and the UGT, revised upwards the trajectory of the national minimum wage. The agreement provides for annual increases of 50 euros, with the aim of reaching 1,020 euros in 2028.
In the civil service, the multi-annual agreement in force provides for pay rises of 2.30% in 2027, with a minimum increase of 60.52 euros.
If the planned rise in the agreement goes ahead, the minimum wage in the public administration should increase to 995.51 euros in 2027.
The agreement also provides for an increase in the meal allowance, currently set at 6.15 euros, of 15 cents a year until 2029.
State guarantees maintained in 2027
The Government has also decided to maintain support for access to first homes, including the public guarantee on mortgage loans and IMT and stamp duty exemptions for young people.
The Government foresees the "continuation" of these measures, specifically "the public guarantee on the purchase of a first home, as well as IMT and stamp duty exemptions on the purchase of a first permanent home".
According to Government data, these measures "have already benefited almost 120,000 young people", with an average purchase price of 200,000 euros.
The public guarantee allows the state to act as guarantor for young people up to the age of 35 when they buy their first home as their main residence. It can cover up to 15% of the initial loan capital, allowing them to obtain 100% financing of the purchase price, without needing an upfront deposit.
The IMT, stamp duty and registry fee exemptions on the purchase of a first home by young people up to the age of 35 have been extended to properties worth up to 338,141 euros.
The Government also plans to strengthen Porta 65, the programme supporting young tenants, although the report does not say by how much the programme's allocation will increase, nor whether there will be changes to the eligibility criteria.
Health budget to fall by 1.5% next year
In the key policy areas, the health budget will total 17,858 million euros next year, 1.5% less than the total amount the Government expects to spend this year.
According to the document, the health programme has a consolidated total expenditure of 17,858.4 million euros for 2027, below the 18,125.9 million euros the Government expects to execute this year, including money from the Recovery and Resilience Plan (PRR).
At least 15.5 billion euros will go to funding the National Health Service, 603.4 million euros (4%) more than estimated for this year.
On the spending side, the largest share of the budget goes on the purchase of goods and services (8.4 billion euros), a line item the Government wants to cut by around 4.2% compared with this year's estimate. Staff costs, the second largest item in health spending, will rise by 5.2% to a total of 8.2 billion euros.
More money for education and science in 2027
Conversely, the Government plans to increase funding for education by 1.5% next year.
The Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation will have 7,787.9 million euros for education, an increase of 1.5% on last year.
The bulk of the budget is earmarked for staff costs, which will rise by 4%, with 6,624.2 million euros to be spent next year.
Defence to reach 2.15% of GDP in 2027
The Government will spend 2.15% of GDP on defence in 2027, exceeding the target agreed with NATO thanks to a boost of more than 800 million euros via the European SAFE instrument for maritime surveillance and cyber defence.
The National Defence Programme has a budget of 3,170.9 million euros, of which 1,537 million euros are earmarked for salaries and military allowances.
Under the Military Programming Law, the main equipment priorities include the purchase of KC-390 and A-29N Super Tucano aircraft for the Air Force, maintenance of the submarine fleet and new offshore patrol vessels for the Navy.
State reform sets aside one million euros for AI
The Ministry for State Reform will have a consolidated total expenditure of 107.6 million euros in 2027. "Excluding PRR-related spending, the allocation comes to 96.8 million euros, representing growth of 27.1% compared with the estimate for 2026," the Budget report states.
Of this 107.6 million euros, the largest share is devoted to digitalisation projects (88 million euros).
For next year, State Reform has also earmarked one million euros for the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). In the document, the Government says it wants to "increase the number of use cases in production linked to the national large language model (LLM) Amália" and to increase the "number of AI solutions in production in the Public Administration supported by the AI Centre of Excellence at ARTE".
The Government adds that "the integration of AI solutions will be promoted in priority areas of the Public Administration, always with impact assessment, proper oversight and respect for the principles of trust, security and accountability".

The Government also projects that public debt will fall to 84.5% of GDP in 2027, three percentage points less than the 87.5% estimated for this year.
The cost of financing public debt will weigh more heavily on the state's accounts, with the bill for interest rising by 23.2% to 8,217 million euros. That is equivalent to 2.4% of GDP, compared with 2% in 2026 and 2025.
Pensions, public-sector wages and debt interest are among the main sources of pressure, alongside tax measures such as the updating of personal income tax brackets, the reduction of the corporate tax rate and housing measures.
Measures on personal, corporate and property taxes
The Minister of Finance said that the 2027 Budget provides for a further cut in personal income tax, through the updating of tax brackets, the specific deduction and the minimum subsistence threshold, mechanisms which by law have to be adjusted.
The PSD/CDS-PP government has decided to lower personal income tax rates in the first to sixth brackets by between 0.3 and 0.5 percentage points, a measure with an estimated impact of 400 million euros, which will already be reflected in withholding tax in 2026.
The reduction will be 0.3 percentage points in the first bracket, 0.5 percentage points from the second to the fifth brackets, and again 0.3 percentage points in the sixth bracket.
The rates remain the same as those presented in September 2026, with retroactive effect.
The proposal also confirms a 3.88% update of personal income tax brackets next year, below the 4.5% pay rise in the private sector set out in the social concertation agreement.
In practice this means there is a risk that the tax burden will increase for taxpayers whose pay rises exceed 3.88%. Anyone earning more may be pushed into a higher tax bracket, paying more tax and seeing all or part of their pay rise eroded.
The minimum income exempt from personal income tax in the 2027 State Budget will track the minimum wage. The annual reference value for the minimum subsistence income is 13,580 euros, which divided by 14 months corresponds to 970 euros, the planned minimum wage in 2027.
Productivity bonuses, performance bonuses, profit-sharing and year-end bonuses will also be exempt from personal income tax "up to a limit of 6% of the worker's annual basic pay", according to the 2027 State Budget proposal.
The Government estimates that corporate tax revenue will fall by 99 million euros in 2027 compared with the projected outturn for 2026, a drop of 1%.
"This trend reflects the 1 percentage point cut in the corporate tax rate, whose impact on revenue should be partially offset by the expected growth in economic activity," the document states.
The revenue impact of the one percentage point cut is 300 million euros.
Last year the general corporate tax rate fell from 20% to 19%, which is the rate applied to companies' 2026 profits.
In 2027 the general rate will be cut by another point, from 19% to 18%, but this rate will apply only to 2027 profits, with an impact on the public finances in 2028.
The Government's goal is to bring the corporate tax rate down to 17% by 2028, cutting it by one percentage point a year. The rate will be 15% on the first 50,000 euros of profit for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
The corporate tax break for companies that increase average wages by at least 4.5% will also remain in place next year.
The proposal includes a 2.3% increase in the brackets of municipal property transfer tax (IMT) on the purchase of an urban property or autonomous unit used exclusively for housing, whether or not it is a primary residence.
The purchase of property up to 108,792 euros in value for use as a primary residence will be exempt from IMT. This represents an increase of 2,446 euros compared with this year's threshold of 106,346 euros.
The Government also expects to raise an extra 300 million euros in taxes in 2027 from anti-fraud measures on fuel approved this year.
The State Budget proposal also envisages a 5.2% increase in receipts from the tax on petroleum products (ISP), reaching 3,796 million euros. The Government attributes this growth to private consumption. For 2026, ISP revenue is expected to be 3,610 million euros.
The Government is also forecasting for 2027 an increase of 139 million euros (8.1%) in revenue from tobacco tax, rising to 1,864 million euros.
Revenue from the tax on alcohol, alcoholic beverages and drinks with added sugar or other sweeteners (IABA) is expected to grow by 27 million euros (7.5%), to 392 million euros.
Minimum income, minimum wage and civil service
The document also confirms a 50-euro increase in the solidarity supplement for the elderly (CSI) in 2027, with the reference amount rising to 720 euros.
The Government's programme envisages this reaching 870 euros in 2029, up from the current 670 euros.
This strengthening of the CSI will have an impact of 100 million euros entered in next year's Budget.
Total social security spending on support for the most vulnerable older people is budgeted at 709 million euros in 2027, 38 million more than the amount budgeted last year.
A rise in the minimum wage from 920 to 970 euros is also planned. The tripartite agreement on pay and economic growth for 2025-2028, signed in October 2024 between the Government, the four employers' confederations and the UGT, revised upwards the trajectory of the national minimum wage. The agreement provides for annual increases of 50 euros, with the aim of reaching 1,020 euros in 2028.
In the civil service, the multi-annual agreement in force provides for pay rises of 2.30% in 2027, with a minimum increase of 60.52 euros.
If the planned rise in the agreement goes ahead, the minimum wage in the public administration should increase to 995.51 euros in 2027.
The agreement also provides for an increase in the meal allowance, currently set at 6.15 euros, of 15 cents a year until 2029.
State guarantees maintained in 2027
The Government has also decided to maintain support for access to first homes, including the public guarantee on mortgage loans and IMT and stamp duty exemptions for young people.
The Government foresees the "continuation" of these measures, specifically "the public guarantee on the purchase of a first home, as well as IMT and stamp duty exemptions on the purchase of a first permanent home".
According to Government data, these measures "have already benefited almost 120,000 young people", with an average purchase price of 200,000 euros.
The public guarantee allows the state to act as guarantor for young people up to the age of 35 when they buy their first home as their main residence. It can cover up to 15% of the initial loan capital, allowing them to obtain 100% financing of the purchase price, without needing an upfront deposit.
The IMT, stamp duty and registry fee exemptions on the purchase of a first home by young people up to the age of 35 have been extended to properties worth up to 338,141 euros.
The Government also plans to strengthen Porta 65, the programme supporting young tenants, although the report does not say by how much the programme's allocation will increase, nor whether there will be changes to the eligibility criteria.
Health budget to fall by 1.5% next year
In the key policy areas, the health budget will total 17,858 million euros next year, 1.5% less than the total amount the Government expects to spend this year.
According to the document, the health programme has a consolidated total expenditure of 17,858.4 million euros for 2027, below the 18,125.9 million euros the Government expects to execute this year, including money from the Recovery and Resilience Plan (PRR).
At least 15.5 billion euros will go to funding the National Health Service, 603.4 million euros (4%) more than estimated for this year.
On the spending side, the largest share of the budget goes on the purchase of goods and services (8.4 billion euros), a line item the Government wants to cut by around 4.2% compared with this year's estimate. Staff costs, the second largest item in health spending, will rise by 5.2% to a total of 8.2 billion euros.
More money for education and science in 2027
Conversely, the Government plans to increase funding for education by 1.5% next year.
The Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation will have 7,787.9 million euros for education, an increase of 1.5% on last year.
The bulk of the budget is earmarked for staff costs, which will rise by 4%, with 6,624.2 million euros to be spent next year.
Defence to reach 2.15% of GDP in 2027
The Government will spend 2.15% of GDP on defence in 2027, exceeding the target agreed with NATO thanks to a boost of more than 800 million euros via the European SAFE instrument for maritime surveillance and cyber defence.
The National Defence Programme has a budget of 3,170.9 million euros, of which 1,537 million euros are earmarked for salaries and military allowances.
Under the Military Programming Law, the main equipment priorities include the purchase of KC-390 and A-29N Super Tucano aircraft for the Air Force, maintenance of the submarine fleet and new offshore patrol vessels for the Navy.
State reform sets aside one million euros for AI
The Ministry for State Reform will have a consolidated total expenditure of 107.6 million euros in 2027. "Excluding PRR-related spending, the allocation comes to 96.8 million euros, representing growth of 27.1% compared with the estimate for 2026," the Budget report states.
Of this 107.6 million euros, the largest share is devoted to digitalisation projects (88 million euros).
For next year, State Reform has also earmarked one million euros for the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). In the document, the Government says it wants to "increase the number of use cases in production linked to the national large language model (LLM) Amália" and to increase the "number of AI solutions in production in the Public Administration supported by the AI Centre of Excellence at ARTE".
The Government adds that "the integration of AI solutions will be promoted in priority areas of the Public Administration, always with impact assessment, proper oversight and respect for the principles of trust, security and accountability".

====================================================================================================

2027 budget reaches parliament with PS support secured
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-08
13:18:50 UTC
22:18:50 KST

The government on Thursday submitted to parliament the 2027 state budget, projecting 2% growth and a surplus of 0.1–0.2% of GDP. Approval is assured, as the PS will abstain in the key vote.
On Thursday afternoon the Government submitted to Parliament the draft State Budget law for 2027, two days before the deadline, after approving it this morning in the Council of Ministers.
The document was handed over by the Minister of Finance, Joaquim Miranda Sarmento, to the Speaker of the Assembly of the Republic, José Pedro Aguiar-Branco.
The third State Budget of Luís Montenegro's government has its passage once again guaranteed by the Socialist Party (PS).
The Socialist leader, José Luís Carneiro, announced last week the intention to abstain in the first overall vote, which takes place on 28 October, after the prime minister, Luís Montenegro, gave assurances on four conditions set by the Socialists: a constitutional review with PS and PSD playing a central role, protection of current and future pensions, funding for investments left unfinished after the RRP, and support for the recovery of municipalities and regions affected by storms.
The detailed debate and vote will run between 29 October and 24 November, with the final overall vote scheduled for 24 November.
The PCP and the Left Bloc have already announced that they will vote against the Government's proposal. Chega has also threatened to vote against (source in Portuguese)if the prime minister refuses to lower the retirement age, and has put forward an additional demand to cut VAT on fuels and apply zero VAT to a basic basket of essential foodstuffs. These are red lines the Government has already rejected.
The remaining parties have not yet announced how they will vote.
The President of the Republic, António José Seguro, said on Thursday that he hoped for a "fruitful debate" to improve people's lives "at a very difficult time".
Speaking to journalists in Parliament after meetings with the parties on the Budget proposal, the Minister of Finance, Joaquim Miranda Sarmento, declined to say how much room there was for negotiations.
The Government estimates that the economic measures already adopted, which will continue to affect the public finances in 2027, will have a impact of 4.8 billion euros next year, still without taking into account any new policies to be included in the next Budget.
As for the macroeconomic scenario for next year, the Government is forecasting economic growth of 2%, in line with the pace seen in recent years, but representing a slight slowdown compared with the 2.3% expected for this year.

The Ministry for State Reform will have a consolidated total expenditure of 107.6 million euros in 2027. "Excluding PRR-related spending, the allocation comes to 96.8 million euros, representing growth of 27.1% compared with the estimate for 2026," the Budget report states.
Of this 107.6 million euros, the largest share is devoted to digitalisation projects (88 million euros).
For next year, State Reform has also earmarked one million euros for the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). In the document, the Government says it wants to "increase the number of use cases in production linked to the national large language model (LLM) Amália" and to increase the "number of AI solutions in production in the Public Administration supported by the AI Centre of Excellence at ARTE".
The Government adds that "the integration of AI solutions will be promoted in priority areas of the Public Administration, always with impact assessment, proper oversight and respect for the principles of trust, security and accountability".
